title.zh: 卷十四 列傳第四 宋宗室及諸王下
title.en: Volume 14 Biographies 4: Members of the Song Imperial Family 2
title.raw: 卷十四 列傳第四 宋宗室及諸王下 Volume 14 Biographies 4: Members of the Song Imperial Family 2

sentences.zh: 列傳第四宋宗室及諸王下

translations.literal: Biographies 4: Song Imperial Family and Princes 2
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 4 — Members of the Song Imperial Family 2

sentences.zh: 宋文帝諸子孝武諸子孝明諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Emperor Wen; sons of Emperor Xiaowu; sons of Emperor Xiaoming
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Emperor Wen; the sons of Emperor Xiaowu; the sons of Emperor Xiaoming

sentences.zh: 文帝十九男：元皇后生元凶劭，潘淑妃生始興王浚，路淑媛生孝武帝，吳淑儀生南平穆王鑠，高修儀生廬陵昭王紹，殷修華生竟陵王誕，曹婕妤生建平宣簡王宏，陳修容生東海王褘，謝容華生晉熙王昶，江修容生武昌王渾，沈婕妤生明帝，楊美人生始安王休仁，邢美人生山陽王休佑，蔡美人生海陵王休茂，董美人生鄱陽哀王休業，顏美人生臨慶沖王休倩，陳美人生新野懷王夷父，荀美人生桂陽王休范，羅美人生巴陵哀王休若。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had nineteen sons: the Primary Empress bore the Crown Prince Assassin Shao; Consort Pan bore Prince of Shixing Jun; Lady Lu bore Emperor Xiaowu; Lady Wu bore Prince Mu of Nanping Shuo; Lady Gao bore Prince Zhao of Luling Shao; Lady Yin bore Prince of Jingling Dan; Lady Cao bore Prince Xuanjian of Jianping Hong; Lady Chen bore Prince of Donghai Hui; Lady Xie bore Prince of Jinxi Chang; Lady Jiang bore Prince of Wuchang Hun; Lady Shen bore Emperor Ming; Lady Yang bore Prince of Shi'an Xiuren; Lady Xing bore Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou; Lady Cai bore Prince of Hailing Xiumao; Lady Dong bore Prince Ai of Poyang Xiuye; Lady Yan bore Prince Chong of Linqing Xiuqian; Lady Chen bore Prince Huai of Xinye Yifu; Lady Xun bore Prince of Guiyang Xiufan; Lady Luo bore Prince Ai of Baling Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had nineteen sons. The primary empress bore the crown prince and regicide Shao. Consort Pan bore Prince Jun of Shixing; Lady Lu bore Emperor Xiaowu; Lady Wu bore Prince Mu of Nanping, Shuo; Lady Gao bore Prince Zhao of Luling, Shao; Lady Yin bore Prince Dan of Jingling; Lady Cao bore Prince Xuanjian of Jianping, Hong; Lady Chen bore Prince Hui of Donghai; Lady Xie bore Prince Chang of Jinxi; Lady Jiang bore Prince Hun of Wuchang; Lady Shen bore Emperor Ming; Lady Yang bore Prince Xiuren of Shi'an; Lady Xing bore Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang; Lady Cai bore Prince Xiumao of Hailing; Lady Dong bore Prince Ai of Poyang, Xiuye; Lady Yan bore Prince Chong of Linqing, Xiuqian; Lady Chen bore Prince Huai of Xinye, Yifu; Lady Xun bore Prince Xiufan of Guiyang; and Lady Luo bore Prince Ai of Baling, Xiuruo.

sentences.zh: 紹出繼廬陵孝獻王義真。

translations.literal: Shao was given out in adoption to succeed Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was given in adoption to succeed Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 元凶劭字休遠，文帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince Assassin Shao, styled Xiuyuan, was Emperor Wen's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and regicide Shao, styled Xiuyuan, was Emperor Wen's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 帝即位後，諒闇中生劭，故秘之。

translations.literal: After the Emperor took the throne, Shao was born during the mourning period, so it was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was born while the emperor was still in mourning after his accession, so the birth was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年閏正月方云劭生。

translations.literal: Only in the intercalary first month of the third year of Yuanjia was Shao's birth announced.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the intercalary first month of Yuanjia 3 was Shao's birth publicly announced.

sentences.zh: 自前代人君即位後，皇后生太子，唯殷帝乙踐阼，正妃生紂，至此又有劭焉。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when a ruler took the throne and the empress bore the crown prince, only when Emperor Yi of Yin ascended and his principal consort bore Zhou did this occur — and now there was Shao as well.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when an emperor had already taken the throne and his empress then bore the crown prince, the only precedent was Emperor Yi of Yin, whose principal consort bore King Zhou — and now Shao stood in the same case.

sentences.zh: 始生三日，帝往視之，簪帽甚堅，無風而墜於劭側，上不悅。

translations.literal: Three days after his birth, when the Emperor came to see him, his hairpin and cap were very secure, yet without wind they fell beside Shao; the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Shao was born, the emperor came to see him. His hairpin and cap were fastened firmly, yet without any wind they fell beside the infant. The emperor took it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 初命之曰劭，在文為召刀，後惡焉，改刀為力。

translations.literal: At first he was named Shao — in writing, "召" plus "刀" — but later, disliking this, he changed the "刀" to "力".
translations.idiomatic: He was first named Shao, written with the character for "summon" plus "knife," but the emperor later disliked that omen and changed the "knife" radical to "strength."

sentences.zh: 年六歲，拜為皇太子，中庶子二率入直永福省，為更築宮，制度嚴麗。

translations.literal: At age six he was appointed crown prince; two leaders of the palace attendants entered duty at Yongfu Palace, and a separate palace was built for him, its regulations strict and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was made crown prince. Two leaders of the palace attendants were posted to Yongfu Palace, a new residence was built for him, and its regulations were made strict and splendid.

sentences.zh: 年十二，出居東宮，納黃門侍郎殷淳女為妃。

translations.literal: At twelve he moved out to the Eastern Palace and took as consort the daughter of Yellow Gate Attendant Officer Yin Chun.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he left the inner palace for the Eastern Palace and married the daughter of Yellow Gate Attendant Officer Yin Chun.

sentences.zh: 十三加元服。

translations.literal: At thirteen he received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he underwent the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 好讀史傳，尤愛弓馬。

translations.literal: He loved reading histories and biographies, and especially loved archery and horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading histories and biographies, and above all loved archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 及長，美鬚眉，大眼方口，長七尺四寸。

translations.literal: When grown, he had handsome brows and beard, large eyes and a square mouth, and stood seven feet four inches tall.
translations.idiomatic: When fully grown he was handsome, with fine brows and beard, large eyes, a square mouth, and a height of seven feet four inches.

sentences.zh: 親覽宮事，延賓客，意之所欲，上必從之。

translations.literal: He personally oversaw palace affairs, received guests, and whatever he desired, the Emperor always granted.
translations.idiomatic: He personally managed palace business, entertained guests, and whatever he wanted the emperor always granted.

sentences.zh: 東宮置兵與羽林等。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace was given troops equal to the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was given a guard force equal to the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，劭拜京陵，大將軍彭城王義康、竟陵王誕、桂陽侯義融並從。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Shao paid respects at the Jingling tombs; Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Prince of Jingling Dan, and Marquis of Guiyang Yirong all accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, Shao paid respects at the imperial tombs at Jingling. Grand General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, Prince Dan of Jingling, and Marquis Yirong of Guiyang all accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上將北侵，劭與蕭思話固諫，不從。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when the Emperor was about to invade the north, Shao and Xiao Sihua firmly remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27, when the emperor planned a northern campaign, Shao and Xiao Sihua remonstrated firmly, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 魏太武帝至瓜步，上登石頭城，有憂色。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei reached Guabu, the Emperor ascended Stone City and wore a worried expression.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei reached Guabu, Emperor Wen climbed Stone City and his face showed worry.

sentences.zh: 劭曰：「不斬江湛、徐湛之，無以謝天下。

translations.literal: Shao said: "If Jiang Zhan and Xu Tanzhi are not executed, there is no way to answer the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Unless Jiang Zhan and Xu Tanzhi are executed, there is no way to answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「北伐自我意，不關二人；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The northern campaign was my own idea and has nothing to do with those two;"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The northern campaign was my own decision and has nothing to do with those two men —"

sentences.zh: 但湛等不異耳。

translations.literal: "but Zhan and the others are no different."
translations.idiomatic: "but Zhan and the others are no different in my eyes."

sentences.zh: 」由是與江、徐不平。

translations.literal: From this he was at odds with Jiang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Shao was estranged from Jiang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 上時務本業，使宮內皆蠶，欲以諷勵天下。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor stressed fundamental industry and had everyone in the palace raise silkworms, intending thereby to admonish and encourage the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then emphasized basic industry and had everyone in the palace raise silkworms, hoping to admonish and encourage the whole realm by example.

sentences.zh: 有女巫嚴道育夫為劫，坐沒入奚官。

translations.literal: There was a shamaness, Yan Daoyu, whose husband had been a bandit and was confiscated into the palace women.
translations.idiomatic: There was a shamaness named Yan Daoyu whose husband had been a bandit; after his conviction she was confiscated into the palace women.

sentences.zh: 劭姊東陽公主應合婢王鸚鵡白公主道育通靈，主乃白上托雲善蠶，求召入。

translations.literal: Shao's elder sister the Princess of Dongyang had a maid Wang Yingwu who told the princess that Daoyu had spirit powers; the princess then told the Emperor, claiming skill in sericulture, and asked that she be summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's elder sister, the Princess of Dongyang, had a maid named Wang Yingwu who told her that Daoyu possessed spirit powers. The princess then told the emperor that Daoyu was skilled at sericulture and asked that she be summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 道育云：「所奉天神，當賜符應。

translations.literal: Daoyu said: "The celestial deity I serve will grant talismanic responses."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu said, "The celestial deity I serve will grant talismanic signs in response."

sentences.zh: 」時主夕臥，見流光相隨，狀若螢火，遂入巾箱化為雙珠，圓青可愛。

translations.literal: That evening the princess lay down to sleep and saw flowing light following her, like fireflies; it entered her kerchief box and turned into paired pearls, round and blue-green and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, as the princess lay down to sleep, she saw flowing light trailing her like fireflies. It entered her kerchief box and turned into a pair of round blue-green pearls.

sentences.zh: 於是主及劭並信惑之。

translations.literal: Thereupon both the princess and Shao came to believe and be deluded.
translations.idiomatic: After that both the princess and Shao came to believe in her and were thoroughly deluded.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚素佞事劭，並多過失，慮上知，使道育祈請，欲令過不上聞。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Jun had always fawned on Shao and had many faults, fearing the Emperor would learn of them; he had Daoyu pray and petition, wishing his faults would not reach the Emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Shixing had always fawned on Shao and had many faults of his own. Fearing the emperor would learn of them, he had Daoyu pray and petition so that his misdeeds would never reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 歌舞咒詛，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Songs, dances, and curses went on day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Songs, dances, and curses went on day and night without stopping.

sentences.zh: 道育輒云：「自上天陳請，必不洩露。

translations.literal: Daoyu would always say: "I have already petitioned Heaven above; it will surely not be leaked."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu always said, "I have already laid the matter before Heaven above; it will surely not leak out."

sentences.zh: 」劭等敬事，號曰天師。

translations.literal: Shao and the others revered and served her, calling her Celestial Master.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and the others revered and served her and called her the Celestial Master.

sentences.zh: 後遂為巫蠱，刻玉為上形像，埋于含章殿前。

translations.literal: Later they even practiced witchcraft and sorcery, carving a jade image of the Emperor and burying it before Hanzhang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later they even turned to witchcraft and sorcery, carving a jade image of the emperor and burying it before Hanzhang Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，東陽公主有奴陳天興，鸚鵡養以為子而與之淫通。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Princess of Dongyang had a slave Chen Tianxing whom Yingwu raised as a son and with whom she had illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Princess of Dongyang had a slave named Chen Tianxing whom Yingwu had raised as a son and with whom she carried on an illicit affair.

sentences.zh: 鸚鵡、天興及寧州所獻黃門慶國並與巫蠱事，劭以天興補隊主。

translations.literal: Yingwu, Tianxing, and Qingguo, a eunuch presented from Ningzhou, were all involved in the witchcraft affair; Shao appointed Tianxing company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yingwu, Tianxing, and Qingguo — a eunuch sent as tribute from Ningzhou — were all involved in the witchcraft affair. Shao appointed Tianxing company commander.

sentences.zh: 東陽主薨，鸚鵡應出嫁，劭慮言語泄，與浚謀之，嫁與浚府佐吳興沈懷遠為妾。

translations.literal: When the Princess of Dongyang died, Yingwu was due to marry out; Shao feared her words would leak and plotted with Jun, marrying her to Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing, a staff officer in Jun's household, as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Dongyang died, Yingwu was due to marry out. Shao feared she would talk and plotted with Jun to marry her to Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing, a staff officer in Jun's household, as concubine.

sentences.zh: 不啟上，慮事泄，因臨賀公主微言之。

translations.literal: Without reporting to the Emperor, fearing the matter would leak, he therefore hinted at it to the Princess of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Without informing the emperor, and fearing the affair would leak, he dropped a hint to the Princess of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 上後知天興領隊，遣閹人奚承祖讓劭曰：「汝間用隊主副儘是奴邪？

translations.literal: Later the Emperor learned Tianxing was company commander and sent the eunuch Xi Chengzu to reproach Shao: "Among the company commanders and deputies you use in secret, are they all slaves?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor learned Tianxing was serving as company commander and sent the eunuch Xi Chengzu to reproach Shao: "Are all the company commanders and deputies you use in secret slaves?"

sentences.zh: 欲嫁者又嫁何處？

translations.literal: "If you want to marry someone off, where will you marry her?"
translations.idiomatic: "And if you want to marry someone off, where exactly will you marry her?"

sentences.zh: 」劭答：「南第昔屬天興求將吏驅使，視形容粗健，便兼隊副；

translations.literal: Shao answered: "The Southern Residence once belonged to Tianxing, who asked for officers and clerks to drive and serve; seeing his build coarse and strong, I made him also company deputy;"
translations.idiomatic: Shao answered, "At the Southern Residence Tianxing once asked for officers and clerks to drive and serve him. Seeing that he was coarse and strong in build, I also made him company deputy —"

sentences.zh: 下人欲嫁者猶未有處。

translations.literal: "as for subordinates who wish to marry, there is still no place arranged."
translations.idiomatic: "as for subordinates who wish to marry, no arrangement has yet been made."

sentences.zh: 」時鸚鵡已嫁懷遠矣。

translations.literal: By then Yingwu had already married Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yingwu had already been married to Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劭懼，書告浚，並使報臨賀主，上若問嫁處，當言未定。

translations.literal: Shao was afraid and wrote to inform Jun, also telling him to notify the Princess of Linhe: if the Emperor asked where she had been married, she should say it was still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Shao grew afraid and wrote to Jun, also telling him to notify the Princess of Linhe: if the emperor asked where Yingwu had been married, she should say it was still undecided.

sentences.zh: 浚答書曰：「啟此事多日，今始來問，當是有感發之者。

translations.literal: Jun replied: "I reported this matter many days ago; that he asks only now means someone must have stirred him up."
translations.idiomatic: Jun wrote back, "I reported this matter many days ago. That he asks only now means someone must have stirred him up."

sentences.zh: 計臨賀故不應翻覆言語，自生寒熱也。

translations.literal: "I reckon the Princess of Linhe surely will not reverse her words and create hot-and-cold trouble herself."
translations.idiomatic: "I reckon the Princess of Linhe will not reverse her words and create trouble for herself."

sentences.zh: 此姥由來挾兩端，難可孤保，正爾自問臨賀冀得審實也。

translations.literal: "This old woman has always played both sides and cannot be trusted alone; I am asking Linhe precisely to get the facts straight."
translations.idiomatic: "That old woman has always played both sides and cannot be trusted alone. I am asking Linhe precisely so we can get the facts straight."

sentences.zh: 其若見問，當作依違答之。

translations.literal: "If she is questioned, she should answer evasively."
translations.idiomatic: "If she is questioned, she should answer evasively."

sentences.zh: 天興先署佞人府位，不審監上當無此簿領，可急宜犍之。

translations.literal: "Tianxing was first registered on the sycophant's household roster; I do not know whether the supervisor above keeps such ledgers — he should be killed at once."
translations.idiomatic: "Tianxing was first registered on the sycophant's household roster. I do not know whether the supervisor above keeps such ledgers — he should be killed at once."

sentences.zh: 殿下已見王未？

translations.literal: "Has Your Highness already seen Wang?"
translations.idiomatic: "Has Your Highness already seen Wang?"

sentences.zh: 宜依此具令嚴自躬上啟聞。

translations.literal: "You should have Yan herself go up and report this in full to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "You should have Yan herself go up and report this in full to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 彼人若為不已，政可促其餘命，或是大慶之漸。

translations.literal: "If that man keeps on as he is, we may as well shorten the rest of his life — or that may be the first step toward great fortune."
translations.idiomatic: "If that man keeps on as he is, we may as well shorten the rest of his life — or that may be the first step toward great fortune."

sentences.zh: 」凡劭、浚相與書類如此。

translations.literal: In general, letters between Shao and Jun were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: In general, letters exchanged between Shao and Jun were all like this.

sentences.zh: 所言皆為名號，謂上為「彼人」，或以為「其」；

translations.literal: What they said used code names: they called the Emperor "that man," or sometimes "he";
translations.idiomatic: What they wrote used code names: they called the emperor "that man," or sometimes simply "he."

sentences.zh: 謂太尉江夏王義恭為「佞人」；

translations.literal: they called Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong "the sycophant";
translations.idiomatic: They called Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia "the sycophant."

sentences.zh: 東陽主第在西掖門外，故云：「南第」。

translations.literal: the Princess of Dongyang's residence was outside the Western Side Gate, hence "Southern Residence."
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Dongyang's residence lay outside the Western Side Gate, hence their term "Southern Residence."

sentences.zh: 王即鸚鵡姓。

translations.literal: "Wang" was Yingwu's surname.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang" was Yingwu's surname.

sentences.zh: 「躬上啟聞。

translations.literal: "Go up and report to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "Go up and report to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」者，令道育上天白天神也。

translations.literal: This meant having Daoyu ascend to report to the celestial deity.
translations.idiomatic: This meant having Daoyu ascend to report to the celestial deity.

sentences.zh: 鸚鵡既適懷遠，慮與天興私通事泄，請劭殺之。

translations.literal: After Yingwu married Huaiyuan, fearing her affair with Tianxing would leak, she asked Shao to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingwu married Huaiyuan, fearing her affair with Tianxing would be exposed, she asked Shao to kill him.

sentences.zh: 劭密使人害天興。

translations.literal: Shao secretly sent men to kill Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shao secretly sent men to kill Tianxing.

sentences.zh: 既而慶國謂往來唯有二人，天興既死，慮將見及，乃以白上。

translations.literal: Then Qingguo, reflecting that only two people had been coming and going and that with Tianxing dead he feared he would be implicated, reported it to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qingguo, reflecting that only two people had been coming and going and that with Tianxing dead he would surely be implicated, reported the affair to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上驚惋，即收鸚鵡家，得劭、浚手書，皆咒詛巫蠱之言。

translations.literal: The Emperor was shocked and grieved; he immediately searched Yingwu's household and obtained letters in Shao's and Jun's own hands, all words of cursing, witchcraft, and sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved. He immediately searched Yingwu's household and obtained letters in Shao's and Jun's own hands — all filled with curses, witchcraft, and sorcery.

sentences.zh: 得所埋上形像于宮內。

translations.literal: They recovered the buried image of the Emperor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered the buried image of the emperor from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 道育叛亡，捕之不得。

translations.literal: Daoyu changed dress and fled; she could not be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu changed dress and fled; she could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 上詰責劭、浚，劭、浚唯陳謝而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor interrogated and reproached Shao and Jun; Shao and Jun only apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor interrogated and reproached Shao and Jun, but they offered only apologies.

sentences.zh: 道育變服為尼，逃匿東宮。

translations.literal: Daoyu disguised herself as a nun and hid in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu disguised herself as a nun and hid in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 浚往京口，又以自隨，或出止人張旿家。

translations.literal: When Jun went to Jingkou he took her with him again, or stayed at the home of one Zhang Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun went to Jingkou he took her with him again, or lodged at the home of a man named Zhang Xu.

sentences.zh: 上謂江夏王義恭曰：「常見典籍有此，謂止書傳空言，不意親睹。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "I have often seen this in the classics and thought it existed only in written tradition; I never expected to witness it myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, "I have often read of such things in the classics and thought they existed only on the page. I never expected to witness them myself."

sentences.zh: 劭南面之日，非復我及汝事。

translations.literal: "When Shao faces south as ruler, it will no longer be a matter for you or me."
translations.idiomatic: "When Shao faces south as ruler, it will no longer be a matter for you or me."

sentences.zh: 汝兒子多，將來遇此不幸耳。」

translations.literal: "You have many sons; in the future they will meet this misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: "You have many sons. In the future they will meet this misfortune."

sentences.zh: 先是二十八年，彗星起畢、昴，入太微，掃帝坐端門，滅翼、軫。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the twenty-eighth year, a comet rose in Bi and Mao, entered Taiwei, swept the emperor's seat and the End Gate, and extinguished in Yi and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in year 28, a comet rose in Bi and Mao, entered Taiwei, swept the emperor's seat and the End Gate, and faded in Yi and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，熒惑逆行守氐，自十一月霖雨連雪，陽光罕曜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Mars moved retrograde and guarded Di; from the eleventh month rain and snow continued in succession, and sunlight rarely appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29, Mars moved retrograde and guarded Di. From the eleventh month rain and snow continued in succession, and sunlight rarely appeared.

sentences.zh: 時道士范材修練形術，是歲自言死期，如期而死。

translations.literal: At the time the Daoist Fan Cai practiced body-refinement arts; that year he declared his own day of death and died on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Daoist Fan Cai practiced body-refinement arts. That year he declared the day of his death and died exactly on schedule.

sentences.zh: 既殯，江夏王疑其仙也，使開棺視之，首如新刎，血流於背，上聞而惡焉。

translations.literal: After the encoffining, Prince of Jiangxia suspected he had become an immortal and had the coffin opened to look; the head was like freshly cut, blood flowed on the back, and when the Emperor heard of it he was disgusted.
translations.idiomatic: After the encoffining, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia suspected Fan had become an immortal and had the coffin opened. The head looked freshly cut and blood flowed down the back. When the emperor heard of it he was disgusted.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，大風飛霰且雷，上憂有竊發，輒加劭兵，東宮實甲萬人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year, great winds blew hail mixed with thunder; the Emperor feared a sudden uprising and repeatedly added troops to Shao's guard — the Eastern Palace in fact had ten thousand armored men.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 30, great winds blew hail mixed with thunder. The emperor feared a sudden uprising and repeatedly added troops to Shao's guard — the Eastern Palace in fact had ten thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 其年二月，浚自京口入朝，當鎮江陵，復載道育還東宮，欲將西上。

translations.literal: That year in the second month, Jun entered court from Jingkou; he was to garrison Jiangling and again carried Daoyu back to the Eastern Palace, intending to take her west.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the second month Jun entered court from Jingkou. He was to garrison Jiangling and again carried Daoyu back to the Eastern Palace, intending to take her west with him.

sentences.zh: 有告上云：「京口人張旿家有一尼服食，出入征北內，似是嚴道育。

translations.literal: Someone reported to the Emperor: "In Jingkou, at the home of Zhang Xu, there is a nun taking medicine and food who goes in and out within the Northern Expedition headquarters — she appears to be Yan Daoyu."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to the emperor, "In Jingkou, at the home of Zhang Xu, there is a nun taking medicine and food who goes in and out within the Northern Expedition headquarters — she appears to be Yan Daoyu."

sentences.zh: 」上使掩得二婢，云：「道育隨征北還都。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent men to seize two maids, who said: "Daoyu followed the Northern Expedition back to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent men to seize two maids, who said, "Daoyu followed the Northern Expedition back to the capital."

sentences.zh: 」上惆悵惋駭，須檢覆，廢劭賜浚死。

translations.literal: The Emperor was sorrowful, startled, and appalled; he was about to investigate further, depose Shao, and grant Jun death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was sorrowful, startled, and appalled. He was about to investigate further, depose Shao, and grant Jun death.

sentences.zh: 初，浚母卒，命潘淑妃養以為子。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jun's mother died, the Emperor ordered Consort Pan to raise him as her son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jun's mother died, the emperor ordered Consort Pan to raise him as her son.

sentences.zh: 淑妃愛浚，浚心不附。

translations.literal: The consort loved Jun, but Jun's heart did not attach to her.
translations.idiomatic: The consort loved Jun, but Jun's heart did not attach to her.

sentences.zh: 妃被寵，上以謀告之。

translations.literal: The consort was favored; the Emperor told her of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was favored, and the emperor told her of the plot.

sentences.zh: 妃以告浚，浚報劭，因有異謀。

translations.literal: The consort told Jun; Jun reported to Shao, and therefore they formed a separate plot.
translations.idiomatic: The consort told Jun, and Jun reported to Shao. From that they formed a separate plot.

sentences.zh: 每夜饗將士，或親自行酒，密與腹心隊主陳叔兒、齋帥張超之、任建之謀之。

translations.literal: Every night he feasted officers and soldiers, sometimes personally going among them with wine, secretly plotting with his trusted company commander Chen Shuer, ritual officer Zhang Chaozhi, and Ren Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Every night he feasted officers and soldiers, sometimes personally going among them with wine, secretly plotting with his trusted company commander Chen Shuer, ritual officer Zhang Chaozhi, and Ren Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 其月二十一日夜，詐作上詔，云：「魯秀謀反，汝可平明率眾入。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-first of that month he forged an imperial edict saying: "Lu Xiu is plotting rebellion; at dawn you may lead the host inside."
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-first of that month he forged an imperial edict saying, "Lu Xiu is plotting rebellion. At dawn you may lead the host inside."

sentences.zh: 」因使超之等集素所養士二千餘人皆被甲，云：「有所討」。

translations.literal: He then had Chaozhi and the others assemble more than two thousand trained retainers, all in armor, saying there was "something to punish."
translations.idiomatic: He then had Chaozhi and the others assemble more than two thousand trained retainers, all in armor, saying there was "something to punish."

sentences.zh: 宿召前中庶子右軍長史蕭斌及左衛率袁淑、中舍人殷仲素、左積弩將軍王正見併入，告以大事，自起拜斌等，因流涕。

translations.literal: Overnight he summoned the former palace attendant, Right Army Chief Clerk Xiao Bin, Left Guard Leader Yuan Shu, Palace Attendant Yin Zhongsu, and Left Crossbow General Wang Zhengjian together, told them of the great affair, rose himself to bow to Bin and the others, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight he summoned the former palace attendant, Right Army Chief Clerk Xiao Bin, Left Guard Leader Yuan Shu, Palace Attendant Yin Zhongsu, and Left Crossbow General Wang Zhengjian together, told them of the great affair, rose himself to bow to Bin and the others, and wept.

sentences.zh: 並驚愕。

translations.literal: They were all startled and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: They were all startled and dismayed.

sentences.zh: 明旦，劭以朱服加戎服上，乘畫輪車，與蕭斌同載，衛從如常入朝儀，從萬春門入。

translations.literal: At dawn Shao wore ceremonial robes over armor, rode in a painted wheel carriage, and rode with Xiao Bin; his escort followed the usual court entry ritual and entered through Wanchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shao wore ceremonial robes over armor, rode in a painted wheel carriage with Xiao Bin, and entered court through Wanchun Gate with escort following the usual ritual.

sentences.zh: 舊制，東宮隊不得入城，劭語門衛云：「受詔有所收討。

translations.literal: By old regulation the Eastern Palace guard could not enter the city; Shao told the gate guards: "I have received an edict to seize and punish someone."
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation the Eastern Palace guard could not enter the city. Shao told the gate guards, "I have received an edict to seize and punish someone."

sentences.zh: 」令後速來，張超之等數十人馳入雲龍東中華門。

translations.literal: He ordered them to follow quickly; several dozen men including Zhang Chaozhi galloped through the Eastern Gate of Cloud Dragon and the Central Gate of China.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them to follow quickly. Several dozen men including Zhang Chaozhi galloped through the Eastern Gate of Cloud Dragon and the Central Gate of China.

sentences.zh: 及齋合，拔刃徑上合殿。

translations.literal: Reaching the ritual hall, they drew blades and went straight up to the Hall of Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the ritual hall, they drew blades and went straight up to the Hall of Audience.

sentences.zh: 上其夜與尚書僕射徐湛之屏人語，至旦燭猶未滅，門階戶席並無侍衛。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor had been speaking privately with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Tanzhi; at dawn the candles were still unextinguished, and there were no attendants at door, step, or couch.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor had been speaking privately with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Tanzhi. At dawn the candles were still burning, and there were no attendants at door, step, or couch.

sentences.zh: 上以幾自鄣，超之行殺，上五指俱落，並殺湛之。

translations.literal: The Emperor used a table to shield himself; Chaozhi went forward and killed him — all five fingers of one hand were cut off — and Xu Tanzhi was killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used a table to shield himself. Chaozhi went forward and killed him — all five fingers of one hand were cut off — and Xu Tanzhi was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 劭進至合殿中合，文帝已崩。

translations.literal: Shao advanced to the inner hall of the Hall of Audience; Emperor Wen was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Shao advanced to the inner hall of the Hall of Audience. Emperor Wen was already dead.

sentences.zh: 出坐東堂，蕭斌執刀侍直，呼中書舍人顧嘏。

translations.literal: He went out and sat in the Eastern Hall; Xiao Bin held a blade and attended upright; he called Palace Attendant Gu Gu.
translations.idiomatic: He went out and sat in the Eastern Hall. Xiao Bin held a blade and attended upright. He called Palace Attendant Gu Gu.

sentences.zh: 嘏懼，不時出，及至，問曰：「欲共見廢，何不早啟。

translations.literal: Gu was afraid and did not come out promptly; when he arrived Shao asked: "You were to witness the deposition together — why did you not report early?"
translations.idiomatic: Gu was afraid and did not come out promptly. When he arrived Shao asked, "You were to witness the deposition together — why did you not report early?"

sentences.zh: 」未及答，斬之。

translations.literal: Before he could answer, he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could answer, he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 遣人於崇禮闥，殺吏部尚書江湛。

translations.literal: He sent men to Chongli Gate to kill Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to Chongli Gate to kill Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zhan.

sentences.zh: 文帝左細仗主卜天與攻劭於東堂，見殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's Left Fine Guard commander Bu Tianyu attacked Shao in the Eastern Hall and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's Left Fine Guard commander Bu Tianyu attacked Shao in the Eastern Hall and was killed.

sentences.zh: 又使人入殺潘淑妃，剖其心觀其邪正。

translations.literal: He also sent men to kill Consort Pan, cut open her heart, and examine whether it was wicked or upright.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to kill Consort Pan, cut open her heart, and examine whether it was wicked or upright.

sentences.zh: 使者阿旨，答曰：「心邪。

translations.literal: The envoy flattered him and answered: "The heart is wicked."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy flattered him and answered, "The heart is wicked."

sentences.zh: 」劭曰：「邪佞之心，故宜邪也。

translations.literal: Shao said: "A wicked and sycophantic heart — of course it should be wicked."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "A wicked and sycophantic heart — of course it should be wicked."

sentences.zh: 」又殺文帝親信左右數十人。

translations.literal: He also killed several dozen of Emperor Wen's trusted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed several dozen of Emperor Wen's trusted attendants.

sentences.zh: 急召始興王浚率眾屯中堂。

translations.literal: He urgently summoned Prince of Shixing Jun to lead troops and encamp in the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently summoned Prince Jun of Shixing to lead troops and encamp in the Central Hall.

sentences.zh: 成服日，劭登殿臨靈，號慟不自持。

translations.literal: On the day mourning garments were donned, Shao ascended the hall to attend the spirit; he wailed and could not control himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the day mourning garments were donned, Shao ascended the hall to attend the spirit and wailed until he could not control himself.

sentences.zh: 博訪公卿，詢求政道，遣使分行四方。

translations.literal: He broadly sought out the high ministers and inquired after the way of governance, sending envoys in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: He broadly sought out the high ministers and inquired after the way of governance, sending envoys in all directions.

sentences.zh: 分浙江以東五郡為會州，省揚州，立司隸校尉，以殷沖補之。

translations.literal: East of the Zhe River he divided five commanderies into Huizhou, abolished Yangzhou, and established the Director of Retainers, appointing Yin Chong to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Zhe River he divided five commanderies into Huizhou, abolished Yangzhou, and established the Director of Retainers, appointing Yin Chong to the post.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍江夏王義恭為太保，司徒南譙王義宣為太尉。

translations.literal: He made Grand General Prince of Jiangxia Yigong Grand Tutor and Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He made Grand General Prince Yigong of Jiangxia Grand Tutor and Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史始興王浚進號驃騎將軍，王僧綽以先豫廢立見誅。

translations.literal: Governor of Jingzhou Prince of Shixing Jun was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry; Wang Sengchuo was executed for having earlier taken part in the plan to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Jingzhou Prince Jun of Shixing was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry. Wang Sengchuo was executed for having earlier taken part in the plan to depose him.

sentences.zh: 長沙王瑾弟楷、臨川王燁、桂陽侯覬、新渝侯玠，並以宿恨死。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Jin's younger brothers Kai and Prince of Linchuan Ye, Marquis of Guiyang Qi, and Marquis of Xinyu Jie all died from old grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin of Changsha's younger brothers Kai and Prince Ye of Linchuan, Marquis Qi of Guiyang, and Marquis Jie of Xinyu all died from old grudges.

sentences.zh: 禮官希旨，諡文帝不敢盡美稱，諡曰中宗景皇帝。

translations.literal: The ritual officers flattered him; in posthumous title for Emperor Wen they dared not use fully laudatory terms and gave the title Emperor Jing of the Middle Founding.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers flattered him. In the posthumous title for Emperor Wen they dared not use fully laudatory terms and gave the title Emperor Jing of the Middle Founding.

sentences.zh: 及聞南譙王義宣、隨王誕等起義師，悉聚諸王於城內。

translations.literal: When he heard Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, Prince of Sui Dan, and others had raised righteous armies, he gathered all the princes within the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao, Prince Dan of Sui, and others had raised righteous armies, he gathered all the princes within the city.

sentences.zh: 移江夏王義恭住尚書下舍，分義恭諸子住侍中下省。

translations.literal: He moved Prince of Jiangxia Yigong to lodge in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing and distributed Yigong's sons to lodge in the lower quarters of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He moved Prince Yigong of Jiangxia to lodge in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing and distributed Yigong's sons to lodge in the lower quarters of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 四月，立妻殷為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he installed his wife Yin as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he installed his wife Yin as empress.

sentences.zh: 孝武檄至，劭自謂素習武事，謂朝士曰：「卿等助我理文書，勿厝意戎陣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu's proclamation arrived, Shao, believing himself skilled in military affairs from of old, told the court gentlemen: "You help me manage documents; do not concern yourselves with the battlefield."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu's proclamation arrived, Shao, believing himself skilled in military affairs from of old, told the court gentlemen, "You help me manage documents. Do not concern yourselves with the battlefield."

sentences.zh: 若有寇難，吾當自出，唯恐賊虜不敢動耳。

translations.literal: "If there is enemy trouble, I shall go out myself — I only fear the bandits will not dare move."
translations.idiomatic: "If there is enemy trouble, I shall go out myself. I only fear the bandits will not dare move."

sentences.zh: 」中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Within and without, strict guard was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without, strict guard was ordered.

sentences.zh: 防孝武世子於侍中省，南譙王義宣諸子於太倉空屋。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's heir was guarded in the Palace Attendants' office; the sons of Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan were kept in empty rooms of the Great Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's heir was guarded in the Palace Attendants' office. The sons of Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao were kept in empty rooms of the Great Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 劭使浚與孝武書，言：「上親禦六師，太保又執鉞臨統，吾與烏羊相尋即道。

translations.literal: Shao had Jun write to Emperor Xiaowu, saying: "The Emperor personally leads the Six Armies; the Grand Tutor also holds the battle-axe and commands in chief. I and Wuyang will meet you on the road shortly."
translations.idiomatic: Shao had Jun write to Emperor Xiaowu, saying, "The emperor personally leads the Six Armies, and the Grand Tutor also holds the battle-axe and commands in chief. I and Wuyang will meet you on the road shortly."

sentences.zh: 上聖恩每厚法師，令在殿內住，想弟欲知消息，故及」。

translations.literal: "The Emperor's sacred grace has always favored the Master of the Law; he is kept within the hall. Thinking you would wish to know news, I therefore mention this."
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor's sacred grace has always favored the Master of the Law, who is kept within the hall. Thinking you would wish to know the news, I therefore mention this."

sentences.zh: 烏羊者，南平王鑠，法師，孝武世子小名也。

translations.literal: "Wuyang" was Prince of Nanping Shuo; "Master of the Law" was the childhood name of Emperor Xiaowu's heir.
translations.idiomatic: "Wuyang" was Prince Shuo of Nanping. "Master of the Law" was the childhood name of Emperor Xiaowu's heir.

sentences.zh: 劭欲殺三鎮士庶家口，江夏王義恭、何尚之說曰：「凡舉大事，不顧家口；

translations.literal: Shao wished to kill the households of the three garrisons' officers and commoners; Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and He Shangzhi urged: "In raising a great affair one does not consider households;"
translations.idiomatic: Shao wished to kill the families of the three garrisons' officers and commoners. Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and He Shangzhi urged, "In raising a great affair one does not consider households —"

sentences.zh: 且多是驅逼。

translations.literal: "moreover most were driven and compelled."
translations.idiomatic: "moreover most were driven and compelled."

sentences.zh: 今忽誅其餘累，政足堅彼意耳。

translations.literal: "If you suddenly execute their remaining dependents, that would only harden their resolve."
translations.idiomatic: "If you suddenly execute their remaining dependents, that would only harden their resolve."

sentences.zh: 」劭乃下書，一無所問。

translations.literal: Shao then issued an edict and questioned no one.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then issued an edict and questioned no one further.

sentences.zh: 浚及蕭斌勸劭勒水軍自上決戰，江夏王義恭慮義兵倉卒，船舫陋小，不宜水戰。

translations.literal: Jun and Xiao Bin urged Shao to lead the navy upstream for a decisive battle; Prince of Jiangxia Yigong feared the righteous army was hasty, the boats small and mean, and unsuited to water combat.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Xiao Bin urged Shao to lead the navy upstream for a decisive battle. Prince Yigong of Jiangxia feared the righteous army was hasty, the boats small and mean, and unsuited to water combat.

sentences.zh: 乃進策以為「宜以近待之，遠出則京師空弱，東軍乘虛，容能為患。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a plan saying: "One should wait for the near enemy; if one goes far out the capital will be empty and weak, and the eastern army may exploit the void and become a trouble."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a plan saying, "One should wait for the near enemy. If one goes far out the capital will be empty and weak, and the eastern army may exploit the void and become a trouble."

sentences.zh: 不如養銳待期」。

translations.literal: "Better to nurture sharpness and wait for the appointed time."
translations.idiomatic: "Better to nurture sharpness and wait for the appointed time."

sentences.zh: 劭善其議。

translations.literal: Shao approved this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Shao approved this counsel.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌厲色曰：「南中郎二十年少，業能建如此大事，豈復可量。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin said sternly: "The Southern Palace Attendant is only twenty years old, yet already able to accomplish such a great affair — how can he still be measured?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin said sternly, "The Southern Palace Attendant is only twenty years old, yet already able to accomplish such a great affair — how can he still be measured?"

sentences.zh: 」劭不納。

translations.literal: Shao did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 疑朝廷舊臣不為之用，厚撫王羅漢、魯秀，悉以兵事委之，多賜珍玩美色以悅其志。

translations.literal: Suspecting old ministers of the court would not serve him, he treated Wang Luohan and Lu Xiu generously and entrusted all military affairs to them, giving many precious objects and beautiful women to please their ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting old ministers of the court would not serve him, he treated Wang Luohan and Lu Xiu generously and entrusted all military affairs to them, giving many precious objects and beautiful women to please their ambitions.

sentences.zh: 羅漢先為南平王鑠右軍參軍，劭以其有將用，故以心膂委焉。

translations.literal: Luohan had earlier been Right Army Attendant Officer to Prince of Nanping Shuo; Shao, seeing his military usefulness, therefore entrusted him as intimate aide.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan had earlier been Right Army Attendant Officer to Prince Shuo of Nanping. Shao, seeing his military usefulness, therefore entrusted him as intimate aide.

sentences.zh: 或勸劭保石頭城者，劭曰：「昔人所以固石頭，俟諸侯勤王耳。

translations.literal: Some urged Shao to hold Stone City; Shao said: "People in the past fortified Stone City to await the feudal lords coming to aid the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Shao to hold Stone City. Shao said, "People in the past fortified Stone City to await the feudal lords coming to aid the throne."

sentences.zh: 我若守此，誰當見救，唯應力戰決之。

translations.literal: "If I hold this place, who will come to save me? I should only fight hard and settle it."
translations.idiomatic: "If I hold this place, who will come to save me? I should only fight hard and settle it."

sentences.zh: 」日日自出行軍，慰勞將士。

translations.literal: Day after day he personally went out to the army, comforting and encouraging officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he personally went out to the army, comforting and encouraging officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 使有司奏立子偉之為皇太子。

translations.literal: He had the relevant office memorialize installing his son Weizhi as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He had the relevant office memorialize installing his son Weizhi as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及義軍至新亭，劭登朱雀門躬自督戰。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Xinting, Shao ascended Vermilion Bird Gate and personally directed the battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army reached Xinting, Shao ascended Vermilion Bird Gate and personally directed the battle.

sentences.zh: 將士懷劭重賞，皆為之力戰。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, cherishing Shao's heavy rewards, all fought for him with force.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers, cherishing Shao's heavy rewards, all fought for him with force.

sentences.zh: 將克，而魯秀打退鼓，軍乃止，為柳元景等所乘，故大敗。

translations.literal: They were about to prevail when Lu Xiu beat the retreat drum; the army then halted and was exploited by Liu Yuanjing and others, and suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to prevail when Lu Xiu beat the retreat drum. The army then halted, was exploited by Liu Yuanjing and others, and suffered great defeat.

sentences.zh: 褚湛之攜二子與檀和之同歸順，劭懼，走還台城。

translations.literal: Chu Tanzhi took his two sons and joined Tan Hezhi in submission; Shao was afraid and fled back to the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Tanzhi took his two sons and joined Tan Hezhi in submission. Shao was afraid and fled back to the palace city.

sentences.zh: 其夜，魯秀又南奔。

translations.literal: That night Lu Xiu fled south again.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lu Xiu fled south again.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，江夏王義恭單馬南奔，劭遣浚殺義恭諸子，以輦迎蔣侯神像于宮內，乞恩，拜為大司馬，封鍾山郡王，蘇侯為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong fled south alone on horseback; Shao sent Jun to kill Yigong's sons, had the carriage bring the image of Lord Jiang into the palace to beg favor, bowed to him as Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him Prince of Zhongshan, and made Lord Su General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia fled south alone on horseback. Shao sent Jun to kill Yigong's sons, had the carriage bring the image of Lord Jiang into the palace to beg favor, bowed to him as Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him Prince of Zhongshan, and made Lord Su General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 使南平王鑠為祝文，罪狀孝武。

translations.literal: He had Prince of Nanping Shuo compose the prayer text listing Emperor Xiaowu's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He had Prince Shuo of Nanping compose the prayer text listing Emperor Xiaowu's crimes.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，臨軒，拜子偉之為皇太子，百官皆戎服，劭獨袞衣，下書大赦，唯孝武、劉義恭、義宣、誕不在原例。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh, facing the hall, he invested Weizhi as crown prince; all officials wore military dress while Shao alone wore imperial robes, issued an edict of general amnesty, but Emperor Xiaowu, Liu Yigong, Yixuan, and Dan were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh, facing the hall, he invested Weizhi as crown prince. All officials wore military dress while Shao alone wore imperial robes, issued an edict of general amnesty, but Emperor Xiaowu, Liu Yigong, Yixuan, and Dan were excluded.

sentences.zh: 五月三日，魯秀等攻大航，鉤得一舶。

translations.literal: On the third day of the fifth month, Lu Xiu and others attacked the Great Crossing and hooked one boat.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the fifth month, Lu Xiu and others attacked the Great Crossing and hooked one boat.

sentences.zh: 王羅漢昏酣作妓，聞官軍已度，驚放仗歸降。

translations.literal: Wang Luohan, drunk and making merry with entertainers, heard the government army had crossed and in alarm dropped his weapons and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luohan, drunk and making merry with entertainers, heard the government army had crossed and in alarm dropped his weapons and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是夜，劭閉守六門，於門內鑿塹立柵，以露車為樓。

translations.literal: That night Shao closed and defended the six gates, dug moats and set palisades inside the gates, and used open wagons as towers.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shao closed and defended the six gates, dug moats and set palisades inside the gates, and used open wagons as towers.

sentences.zh: 城內沸亂，將吏並踰城出奔。

translations.literal: Within the city there was boiling disorder; officers and clerks all climbed over the walls and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city there was boiling disorder. Officers and clerks all climbed over the walls and fled.

sentences.zh: 劭使詹叔兒燒輦及袞冕服。

translations.literal: Shao had Zhan Shuer burn the imperial carriages and imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had Zhan Shuer burn the imperial carriages and imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌聞大航不守，惶窘不知所為，宣令所統皆使解甲，尋戴白幡來降，即於軍門伏誅。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin, hearing the Great Crossing was lost, was alarmed and did not know what to do; he proclaimed to those under his command to lay down arms, then came wearing white banners to surrender and was immediately executed at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin, hearing the Great Crossing was lost, was alarmed and did not know what to do. He proclaimed to those under his command to lay down arms, then came wearing white banners to surrender and was immediately executed at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 四日，劭腹心白直諸同逆先屯閶闔門外，並走還入殿。

translations.literal: On the fourth day, Shao's trusted white-guard fellow conspirators who had first encamped outside Changhe Gate all fled back into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day, Shao's trusted white-guard fellow conspirators who had first encamped outside Changhe Gate all fled back into the hall.

sentences.zh: 程天祚與薛安都副譚金因而乘之，即得俱入。

translations.literal: Cheng Tianzuo and Xue Andu, deputy to Tan Jin, exploited this and entered together.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tianzuo and Xue Andu, deputy to Tan Jin, exploited this and entered together.

sentences.zh: 臧質從廣莫門入，同會太極殿前。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi entered from Guangmo Gate and joined them before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi entered from Guangmo Gate and joined them before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 即斬太子左衛率王正見，建平、東海等七王並號哭俱出。

translations.literal: They immediately beheaded Left Guard Leader Wang Zhengjian; the seven princes of Jianping, Donghai, and others all wailed and came out together.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately beheaded Left Guard Leader Wang Zhengjian. The seven princes of Jianping, Donghai, and others all wailed and came out together.

sentences.zh: 劭穿西垣入武庫井中，副隊高禽執之。

translations.literal: Shao broke through the western wall and entered the armory well; Deputy Company Commander Gao Qin seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao broke through the western wall and entered the armory well. Deputy Company Commander Gao Qin seized him.

sentences.zh: 浚率左右數十人，與南平王鑠於西明門出，俱南奔，於越城遇江夏王義恭。

translations.literal: Jun led several dozen followers and Prince of Nanping Shuo out through Ximing Gate; both fled south, and at Yue City met Prince of Jiangxia Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led several dozen followers and Prince Shuo of Nanping out through Ximing Gate. Both fled south, and at Yue City met Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 浚下馬，曰：「南中郎今何在？

translations.literal: Jun dismounted and said: "Where is the Southern Palace Attendant now?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun dismounted and said, "Where is the Southern Palace Attendant now?"

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「已君臨萬國。

translations.literal: Yigong said: "He already rules the myriad states."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "He already rules the myriad states."

sentences.zh: 」又稱字曰：「虎頭來，得無晚乎？

translations.literal: He also used his style name and said: "Hutou has come — isn't it rather late?"
translations.idiomatic: He also used his style name and said, "Hutou has come — isn't it rather late?"

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「恨晚。

translations.literal: Yigong said: "I regret it is late."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "I regret it is late."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「故當不死？

translations.literal: He also said: "So I should not die after all?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "So I should not die after all?"

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「可詣行闕請罪。

translations.literal: Yigong said: "You may go to the traveling palace and beg forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "You may go to the traveling palace and beg forgiveness."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「未審猶能得一職自效不？

translations.literal: He also said: "I wonder whether I can still obtain some post to prove myself?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I wonder whether I can still obtain some post to prove myself?"

sentences.zh: 」義恭又曰：「此未可量。

translations.literal: Yigong again said: "That cannot yet be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong again said, "That cannot yet be measured."

sentences.zh: 」勒與俱自歸，命於馬上斬首。

translations.literal: He compelled Jun to return with him in submission and ordered him beheaded on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: He compelled Jun to return with him in submission and ordered him beheaded on horseback.

sentences.zh: 浚字休明，將產之夕，有鵩鳴於屋上，聞者莫不惡之。

translations.literal: Jun, styled Xiuming, on the night he was about to be born a owl screeched on the roof; all who heard it regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Xiuming, on the night he was about to be born an owl screeched on the roof. All who heard it regarded it as ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，年八歲，封始興王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, at age eight, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 13, at age eight, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 浚少好文籍，資質端妍，母潘淑妃有盛寵。

translations.literal: Jun from youth loved literary works; his talent and bearing were refined and handsome; his mother Consort Pan enjoyed great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jun from youth loved literary works. His talent and bearing were refined and handsome, and his mother Consort Pan enjoyed great favor.

sentences.zh: 時六宮無主，潘專總內政。

translations.literal: At the time the six palaces had no mistress; Pan alone controlled inner administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the six palaces had no mistress. Pan alone controlled inner administration.

sentences.zh: 浚人才既美，母又至愛，文帝甚所留心。

translations.literal: Jun's talent was already beautiful and his mother deeply loved; Emperor Wen greatly attended to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's talent was already beautiful and his mother deeply loved. Emperor Wen greatly attended to him.

sentences.zh: 與建平王宏、侍中王僧綽、中書郎蔡興宗等，並以文義往復。

translations.literal: With Prince of Jianping Hong, Palace Attendant Wang Sengchuo, Secretariat Gentleman Cai Xingzong, and others he exchanged on literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Hong of Jianping, Palace Attendant Wang Sengchuo, Secretariat Gentleman Cai Xingzong, and others he exchanged on literary meaning.

sentences.zh: 初元皇后性忌，以潘氏見幸，恚恨致崩。

translations.literal: Earlier the Primary Empress was jealous by nature; because Pan was favored she resented it and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the primary empress was jealous by nature. Because Pan was favored she resented it and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 故劭深病潘氏及浚。

translations.literal: Therefore Shao deeply hated Pan and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Shao deeply hated Pan and Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚慮將來受禍，乃曲意事劭，劭與之遂善。

translations.literal: Jun feared future calamity and therefore bent his will to serve Shao; Shao and he then became close.
translations.idiomatic: Jun feared future calamity and therefore bent his will to serve Shao. Shao and he then became close.

sentences.zh: 多有過失，屢為上所讓，憂懼，乃與劭共為巫蠱。

translations.literal: He had many faults and was repeatedly reproached by the Emperor; in worry and fear he joined Shao in witchcraft and sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: He had many faults and was repeatedly reproached by the emperor. In worry and fear he joined Shao in witchcraft and sorcery.

sentences.zh: 後出鎮京口，乃因員外散騎侍郎徐爰求鎮江陵，又求助於尚書僕射徐湛之。

translations.literal: Later when he went out to garrison Jingkou he therefore through Supernumerary Palace Cadet Xu Ai sought to garrison Jiangling, and also sought help from Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later when he went out to garrison Jingkou he therefore through Supernumerary Palace Cadet Xu Ai sought to garrison Jiangling, and also sought help from Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 而尚書令何尚之等咸謂浚太子次弟，不應遠出。

translations.literal: But Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi and others all said Jun was the crown prince's next younger brother and should not go far away.
translations.idiomatic: But Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi and others all said Jun was the crown prince's next younger brother and should not go far away.

sentences.zh: 上以上流之重，宜有至親，故以浚為衛將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史，加都督，領護南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the upper Yangzi was weighty, should have the closest kin, therefore made Jun General of the Guard, Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat, and Governor of Jingzhou, with added overall command, holding Protector of the Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because the upper Yangzi was weighty and should have the closest kin, therefore made Jun General of the Guard, Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat, and governor of Jingzhou, with added overall command, holding Protector of the Southern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 浚入朝，遣還京口，為行留處分。

translations.literal: Jun entered court and was sent back to Jingkou to arrange matters before departure.
translations.idiomatic: Jun entered court and was sent back to Jingkou to arrange matters before departure.

sentences.zh: 至京口數日而巫蠱事發，時二十九年七月也。

translations.literal: Several days after reaching Jingkou the witchcraft affair broke out — it was the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after reaching Jingkou the witchcraft affair broke out — it was the seventh month of year 29.

sentences.zh: 上惋歎彌日，謂潘淑妃曰：「太子圖富貴，更是一理，虎頭復如此，非復思慮所及。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in grief for days and said to Consort Pan: "The crown prince scheming for wealth and rank is one thing, but Hutou again like this — it is no longer within what thought can reach."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in grief for days and said to Consort Pan, "The crown prince scheming for wealth and rank is one thing, but Hutou again like this — it is no longer within what thought can reach."

sentences.zh: 汝母子豈可一日無我邪？

translations.literal: "Can you mother and son go a single day without me?"
translations.idiomatic: "Can you mother and son go a single day without me?"

sentences.zh: 」明年荊州事方行。

translations.literal: The next year the Jingzhou appointment was just proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Jingzhou appointment was just proceeding.

sentences.zh: 二月，浚還朝。

translations.literal: In the second month Jun returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Jun returned to court.

sentences.zh: 十四日，臨軒受拜。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day he received investiture facing the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day he received investiture facing the hall.

sentences.zh: 其日，藏嚴道育事發，明旦浚入謝，上容色非常，其夕即加詰問。

translations.literal: That day the matter of hiding Yan Daoyu broke out; the next morning Jun entered to apologize; the Emperor's expression was very strange, and that evening he was closely interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: That day the matter of hiding Yan Daoyu broke out. The next morning Jun entered to apologize. The emperor's expression was very strange, and that evening he was closely interrogated.

sentences.zh: 浚唯謝罪。

translations.literal: Jun only apologized for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Jun only apologized for his crime.

sentences.zh: 潘淑妃抱浚泣曰：「汝始咒詛事發，猶冀刻己思愆，何意忽藏嚴道育。

translations.literal: Consort Pan embraced Jun and wept: "When the cursing affair first broke out I still hoped you would carve yourself and reflect on fault — who expected you would suddenly hide Yan Daoyu?"
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan embraced Jun and wept, "When the cursing affair first broke out I still hoped you would carve yourself and reflect on fault — who expected you would suddenly hide Yan Daoyu?"

sentences.zh: 今日用活何為，可送藥來，吾當先自取盡，不忍見汝禍敗。

translations.literal: "What use is life today? Send poison — I shall first take it all myself. I cannot bear to see your ruin."
translations.idiomatic: "What use is life today? Send poison — I shall first take it all myself. I cannot bear to see your ruin."

sentences.zh: 」浚奮衣去，曰：「天下事尋自判，必不上累。」

translations.literal: Jun shook off his robes and left, saying: "The realm's affairs will soon decide themselves — I shall surely not drag you down."
translations.idiomatic: Jun shook off his robes and left, saying, "The realm's affairs will soon decide themselves — I shall surely not drag you down."

sentences.zh: 劭入弑之旦，浚在西州。

translations.literal: On the morning Shao entered to assassinate, Jun was at the Western Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning Shao entered to assassinate, Jun was at the Western Quarter.

sentences.zh: 府舍人朱法瑜曰：「台內叫喚，宮門皆閉，道上傳太子反，未測禍變所至。

translations.literal: Household officer Zhu Fayu said: "Within the palace there is shouting; the palace gates are all closed; on the road they say the crown prince has rebelled — the calamity and change cannot yet be known."
translations.idiomatic: Household officer Zhu Fayu said, "Within the palace there is shouting. The palace gates are all closed. On the road they say the crown prince has rebelled — the calamity and change cannot yet be known."

sentences.zh: 」浚陽驚曰：「今當奈何。

translations.literal: Jun pretended alarm and said: "What are we to do now?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun pretended alarm and said, "What are we to do now?"

sentences.zh: 」浚未得劭信，不知事之濟不，騷擾不知所為。

translations.literal: Jun had not yet received Shao's message and did not know whether the affair had succeeded; he was agitated and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had not yet received Shao's message and did not know whether the affair had succeeded. He was agitated and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 將軍王慶曰：「今宮內有變，未知主上安危，預在臣子，當投袂赴難。

translations.literal: General Wang Qing said: "Now there is change within the palace; the sovereign's safety is unknown — as subjects we should throw up our sleeves and rush to the crisis."
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Qing said, "Now there is change within the palace. The sovereign's safety is unknown — as subjects we should throw up our sleeves and rush to the crisis."

sentences.zh: 」浚不聽。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄而劭遣張超之馳馬召浚，浚問狀訖，即戎服乘馬而去。

translations.literal: Shortly Shao sent Zhang Chaozhi galloping on horseback to summon Jun; Jun asked how things stood and immediately donned armor, mounted, and went.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly Shao sent Zhang Chaozhi galloping on horseback to summon Jun. Jun asked how things stood and immediately donned armor, mounted, and went.

sentences.zh: 朱法瑜固止浚，浚不從。

translations.literal: Zhu Fayu firmly stopped Jun; Jun would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fayu firmly stopped Jun, but Jun would not heed.

sentences.zh: 至中門，王慶又諫不宜從逆。

translations.literal: At the middle gate Wang Qing again remonstrated that he should not follow rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the middle gate Wang Qing again remonstrated that he should not follow rebellion.

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「皇太子令，敢有復言者斬。

translations.literal: Jun said: "By the crown prince's order — whoever speaks again shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "By the crown prince's order — whoever speaks again shall be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」及入見劭，勸殺荀赤松等。

translations.literal: When he entered and saw Shao, he urged killing Xun Chisong and others.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered and saw Shao, he urged killing Xun Chisong and others.

sentences.zh: 劭謂浚曰：「潘淑妃遂為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Shao told Jun: "Consort Pan was then killed by mutinous soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Shao told Jun, "Consort Pan was then killed by mutinous soldiers."

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「此是下情由來所願。

translations.literal: Jun said: "That is what the lower feelings have long wished."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "That is what the lower feelings have long wished."

sentences.zh: 」其悖逆如此。

translations.literal: His rebellion was to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: His rebellion was to this degree.

sentences.zh: 劭將敗，勸劭入海，輦珍寶繒帛下船。

translations.literal: When Shao was about to be defeated, he urged Shao to flee to sea; they loaded precious objects and silks onto boats.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao was about to be defeated, he urged Shao to flee to sea. They loaded precious objects and silks onto boats.

sentences.zh: 及劭入井，高禽于井出之。

translations.literal: When Shao entered the well, Gao Qin pulled him out from the well.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao entered the well, Gao Qin pulled him out from the well.

sentences.zh: 劭問天子何在，禽曰：「至尊近在新亭。

translations.literal: Shao asked where the Son of Heaven was; Qin said: "His Majesty is recently at Xinting."
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked where the Son of Heaven was. Qin said, "His Majesty is recently at Xinting."

sentences.zh: 」將劭至殿前，臧質見之慟哭。

translations.literal: They brought Shao before the hall; Zang Zhi saw him and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: They brought Shao before the hall. Zang Zhi saw him and wailed.

sentences.zh: 劭曰：「天地所不覆載，丈人何為見哭。

translations.literal: Shao said: "What Heaven and Earth do not cover and bear — Elder, why weep for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "What Heaven and Earth do not cover and bear — Elder, why weep for me?"

sentences.zh: 」質因辨其逆狀，答曰：「先朝當見枉廢，不能作獄中囚。

translations.literal: Zhi therefore set forth his rebellious conduct; he answered: "The former emperor should have been wrongly deposed; I could not become a prisoner in jail."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi therefore set forth his rebellious conduct. Shao answered, "The former emperor should have been wrongly deposed. I could not become a prisoner in jail."

sentences.zh: 問計于蕭斌，斌見勸如此。

translations.literal: "I asked counsel of Xiao Bin; Bin saw and urged thus."
translations.idiomatic: "I asked counsel of Xiao Bin. Bin saw and urged thus."

sentences.zh: 」又語質曰：「可得為乞遠徙不？

translations.literal: He also said to Zhi: "Can you beg exile far away for me?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Zhi, "Can you beg exile far away for me?"

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「主上近在航南，自當有處分。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "The sovereign is recently south of the Crossing; he himself will have disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "The sovereign is recently south of the Crossing. He himself will have disposition."

sentences.zh: 」縛劭馬上，防送軍門。

translations.literal: They bound Shao on horseback and escorted him under guard to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Shao on horseback and escorted him under guard to the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 及至牙下，據鞍顧望。

translations.literal: When he reached below the headquarters he leaned on the saddle and looked back.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached below the headquarters he leaned on the saddle and looked back.

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭與諸王共臨視之，義恭曰：「我背逆歸順，有何大罪，頓殺十二兒。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and the princes together viewed him; Yigong said: "I turned from rebellion to submission — what great crime is there, that you instantly killed twelve sons?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and the princes together viewed him. Yigong said, "I turned from rebellion to submission — what great crime is there, that you instantly killed twelve sons?"

sentences.zh: 」劭曰：「殺諸弟此一事負阿父。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Killing the younger brothers — in this one matter I wronged Uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Killing the younger brothers — in this one matter I wronged Uncle."

sentences.zh: 」江湛妻庾氏乘車罵之，龐秀之亦加誚讓。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan's wife Lady Yu rode in a carriage and cursed him; Pang Xiuzhi also added reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan's wife Lady Yu rode in a carriage and cursed him. Pang Xiuzhi also added reproach.

sentences.zh: 劭厲聲曰：「汝輩復何煩爾。

translations.literal: Shao said harshly: "Why do you people trouble yourselves so?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao said harshly, "Why do you people trouble yourselves so?"

sentences.zh: 」先殺其四子，語南平王鑠曰：「此何有哉。

translations.literal: He first killed his four sons and said to Prince of Nanping Shuo: "What is there in this?"
translations.idiomatic: He first killed his four sons and said to Prince Shuo of Nanping, "What is there in this?"

sentences.zh: 」乃斬於牙下。

translations.literal: Then he was beheaded below the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then he was beheaded below the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 臨刑歎曰：「不圖宋室一至於此。

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed: "I never thought the Song house would come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he sighed, "I never thought the Song house would come to this."

sentences.zh: 」劭、浚及其子並梟首大航，暴屍於市。

translations.literal: Shao, Jun, and their sons all had heads displayed at the Great Crossing; corpses were exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, Jun, and their sons all had heads displayed at the Great Crossing. Corpses were exposed in the market.

sentences.zh: 劭妻殷氏賜死于廷尉，臨刑謂獄丞江恪曰：「汝家骨肉相殘，何以枉殺天下無罪人。

translations.literal: Shao's wife Lady Yin was granted death at the Court Commandant; facing execution she told Prison Director Jiang Ke: "Your house slaughters its own flesh and blood — why wrongly kill innocent people under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao's wife Lady Yin was granted death at the Court Commandant. Facing execution she told Prison Director Jiang Ke, "Your house slaughters its own flesh and blood — why wrongly kill innocent people under Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「受拜皇后，非罪而何。

translations.literal: Ke said: "Receiving appointment as empress — if not a crime, what is?"
translations.idiomatic: Ke said, "Receiving appointment as empress — if not a crime, what is?"

sentences.zh: 」殷氏曰：「此權時耳，當以鸚鵡為後也。

translations.literal: Lady Yin said: "That was only for the moment — Yingwu was to be empress afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin said, "That was only for the moment — Yingwu was to be empress afterward."

sentences.zh: 」浚妻褚氏，丹陽尹湛之之女。

translations.literal: Jun's wife Lady Chu was the daughter of Governor of Danyang Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's wife Lady Chu was the daughter of Governor of Danyang Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 湛之南奔之始，即見離絕，故免於誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tanzhi's flight south he was already separated from her, and therefore she escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tanzhi's flight south he was already separated from her, and therefore she escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 其餘子女妾媵並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: The remaining sons, daughters, concubines, and attendants were all granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining sons, daughters, concubines, and attendants were all granted death in prison.

sentences.zh: 投劭、浚屍首于江，其餘同逆及王羅漢等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Shao's and Jun's corpses were thrown into the river; the remaining fellow conspirators and Wang Luohan and others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's and Jun's corpses were thrown into the river. The remaining fellow conspirators and Wang Luohan and others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 張超之聞兵入，遂至合殿故基，止於御床之所，為亂兵所殺，剖腹刳心，臠割其肉，諸將生噉之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chaozhi, hearing troops had entered, went to the old foundation of the Hall of Audience and stopped at the place of the imperial couch; mutinous soldiers killed him, cut open his belly and scooped out his heart, sliced his flesh, and the generals ate it raw.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chaozhi, hearing troops had entered, went to the old foundation of the Hall of Audience and stopped at the place of the imperial couch. Mutinous soldiers killed him, cut open his belly and scooped out his heart, sliced his flesh, and the generals ate it raw.

sentences.zh: 焚其頭骨。

translations.literal: They burned his skull.
translations.idiomatic: They burned his skull.

sentences.zh: 時不見傳國璽，問劭，雲在嚴道育處。

translations.literal: At the time the transmission seal was not seen; Shao was asked and said it was with Yan Daoyu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the transmission seal was not seen. Shao was asked and said it was with Yan Daoyu.

sentences.zh: 就取得之。

translations.literal: They went and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: They went and obtained it.

sentences.zh: 道育、鸚鵡並都街鞭殺，於石頭四望山焚其屍，揚灰于江。

translations.literal: Daoyu and Yingwu were both whipped to death in the capital street; at Siwang Mountain in Stone City their corpses were burned and ashes scattered in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu and Yingwu were both whipped to death in the capital street. At Siwang Mountain in Stone City their corpses were burned and ashes scattered in the river.

sentences.zh: 毀劭東宮所住齋，汙瀦其處。

translations.literal: They destroyed the ritual hall where Shao's Eastern Palace had dwelt and defiled the place as a cesspool.
translations.idiomatic: They destroyed the ritual hall where Shao's Eastern Palace had dwelt and defiled the place as a cesspool.

sentences.zh: 封高禽新陽縣男。

translations.literal: Gao Qin was enfeoffed Baron of Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qin was enfeoffed Baron of Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 追贈潘淑妃為長寧園夫人，置守塚。

translations.literal: Consort Pan was posthumously granted Lady of Changning Garden and given tomb guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan was posthumously granted Lady of Changning Garden and given tomb guardians.

sentences.zh: 偽司隸校尉殷沖、丹陽尹尹弘並賜死。

translations.literal: The false Director of Retainers Yin Chong and Governor of Danyang Yin Hong were both granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The false Director of Retainers Yin Chong and Governor of Danyang Yin Hong were both granted death.

sentences.zh: 沖為劭草立符文，又妃叔父；

translations.literal: Chong drafted the installation edicts for Shao and was also the empress's uncle;
translations.idiomatic: Chong drafted the installation edicts for Shao and was also the empress's uncle.

sentences.zh: 弘為劭簡配兵士，盡其心力故也。

translations.literal: Hong selected and assigned soldiers for Shao and exhausted his heart and strength — for these reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Hong selected and assigned soldiers for Shao and exhausted his heart and strength — for these reasons.

sentences.zh: 南平穆王鑠字休玄，文帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Nanping Shuo, styled Xiuxuan, was Emperor Wen's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu of Nanping, Shuo, styled Xiuxuan, was Emperor Wen's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十六年，年九歲，封南平王，少好學，有文才，未弱冠，擬古三十餘首，時人以為亞跡陸機。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, at age nine, he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanping; from youth he loved learning and had literary talent; before weak-capping he composed more than thirty pieces in the ancient style — contemporaries thought him second only to Lu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 16, at age nine, he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanping. From youth he loved learning and had literary talent. Before weak-capping he composed more than thirty pieces in the ancient style — contemporaries thought him second only to Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為南豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he became Governor of South Yu Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he became governor of South Yu Province, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 時文帝方事外略，罷南豫州並壽陽，以鑠為豫州刺史，領安蠻校尉。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wen was engaged in external campaigns; he abolished South Yu Province together with Shouyang and made Shuo Governor of Yu Province, holding Protector of the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Wen was engaged in external campaigns. He abolished South Yu Province together with Shouyang and made Shuo governor of Yu Province, holding Protector of the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，魏太武圍汝南懸瓠城，行汝南太守陳憲保城自固，魏作高樓施弩射城內，城內負戶以汲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Emperor Taiwu of Wei besieged Xuannao city in Runan; Acting Governor of Runan Chen Xian defended the city and held firm; Wei built high towers and mounted crossbows to shoot into the city, and within the city people carried doors on their backs to draw water.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 Emperor Taiwu of Wei besieged Xuannao city in Runan. Acting Governor of Runan Chen Xian defended the city and held firm. Wei built high towers and mounted crossbows to shoot into the city, and within the city people carried doors on their backs to draw water.

sentences.zh: 又毀佛圖，取金像以為大鉤，施之沖車端以牽樓堞。

translations.literal: They also destroyed Buddhist pagodas, took golden images to make great hooks, and set them at the ends of battering rams to pull down parapets.
translations.idiomatic: They also destroyed Buddhist pagodas, took golden images to make great hooks, and set them at the ends of battering rams to pull down parapets.

sentences.zh: 城內有一沙門頗有機思，輒設奇以應之。

translations.literal: Within the city was a monk of considerable ingenuity who always devised strange responses.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city was a monk of considerable ingenuity who always devised strange responses.

sentences.zh: 魏人以蝦蟆車填塹，肉薄攻城，死者與城等，遂登屍以陵城。
