translations.literal: The Wei people used toad wagons to fill the moat, pressed close flesh-to-flesh to attack the city; the dead equaled the height of the wall, and they climbed corpses to scale the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei people used toad wagons to fill the moat and pressed close flesh-to-flesh to attack the city. The dead equaled the height of the wall, and they climbed corpses to scale the city.

sentences.zh: 憲銳氣愈奮，戰士無不一當百，殺傷萬計，汝水為之不流。

translations.literal: Xian's sharp spirit grew ever fiercer; warriors were none who did not match one hundred; killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands, and the Ru River ceased to flow for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's sharp spirit grew ever fiercer. Warriors were none who did not match one hundred. Killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands, and the Ru River ceased to flow for it.

sentences.zh: 相拒四十餘日，鑠遣安蠻司馬劉康祖與甯朔將軍臧質救之，魏人燒攻具而退。

translations.literal: They resisted more than forty days; Shuo sent Protector of the Barbarians Marshal Liu Kangzu and General of Pacifying the North Zang Zhi to rescue them; the Wei people burned their siege engines and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They resisted more than forty days. Shuo sent Protector of the Barbarians Marshal Liu Kangzu and General of Pacifying the North Zang Zhi to rescue them. The Wei people burned their siege engines and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以鑠為侍中、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Assassin usurped the throne, Shuo was made Palace Attendant and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince assassin usurped the throne, Shuo was made Palace Attendant and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 劭迎蔣侯神于宮內，疏孝武年諱厭咒，祈請假授位號，使鑠造策文。

translations.literal: Shao welcomed Lord Jiang's spirit into the palace, listed tabooed and cursed years of Emperor Xiaowu, prayed and petitioned for borrowed titles, and had Shuo compose the installation text.
translations.idiomatic: Shao welcomed Lord Jiang's spirit into the palace, listed tabooed and cursed years of Emperor Xiaowu, prayed and petitioned for borrowed titles, and had Shuo compose the installation text.

sentences.zh: 及義軍入宮，鑠與浚俱歸孝武。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the palace, Shuo and Jun both submitted to Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army entered the palace, Shuo and Jun both submitted to Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 浚即伏法。

translations.literal: Jun was immediately executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was immediately executed by law.

sentences.zh: 上迎鑠入宮，當時倉卒失國璽，事寧更鑄給之。

translations.literal: The Emperor welcomed Shuo into the palace; at the time in haste the transmission seal was lost; when affairs settled a new one was cast and given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed Shuo into the palace. At the time in haste the transmission seal was lost. When affairs settled a new one was cast and given.

sentences.zh: 進侍中、司空，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: He was promoted Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Works, with troops assigned and staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Works, with troops assigned and staff appointed.

sentences.zh: 以國哀未闋，讓侍中。

translations.literal: Because national mourning was not yet ended, he declined Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because national mourning was not yet ended, he declined Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕字休文，文帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingling Dan, styled Xiuwen, was Emperor Wen's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Jingling, styled Xiuwen, was Emperor Wen's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，年十一，封廣陵王。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 20, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，為雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he became Governor of Yong Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he became governor of Yong Province, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 以廣陵凋弊，改封隨郡王。

translations.literal: Because Guangling was wasted and impoverished, he was changed to Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangling was wasted and impoverished, he was changed to Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 上欲大舉侵魏，以襄陽外接關河，欲廣其資力，乃罷江州軍府，文武悉配雍州，湘州入台租稅雜物，悉給襄陽，及大舉北侵，命諸藩並出師，皆奔敗，唯誕遣中兵參軍柳元景克弘農、關、陝。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to invade Wei on a large scale; because Xiangyang bordered the passes and rivers externally, he wished to expand its strength — he therefore abolished Jiangzhou's military office, assigned all civil and military officers to Yong Province, gave Xiangzhou's tribute rents and miscellaneous goods to the capital, and when the great northern invasion was ordered all the feudatories went out with armies but all fled in defeat; only Dan sent Army Attendant Liu Yuanjing to take Hongnong, Guan, and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to invade Wei on a large scale. Because Xiangyang bordered the passes and rivers externally, he wished to expand its strength — he therefore abolished Jiangzhou's military office, assigned all civil and military officers to Yong Province, gave Xiangzhou's tribute rents and miscellaneous goods to the capital, and when the great northern invasion was ordered all the feudatories went out with armies but all fled in defeat. Only Dan sent Army Attendant Liu Yuanjing to take Hongnong, Guan, and Shan.

sentences.zh: 元凶立，以揚州浙江西屬司隸校尉，浙江東五郡立會州，以誕為刺史。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Assassin established himself, west of the Zhe River in Yang Province was placed under the Director of Retainers; the five commanderies east of the Zhe were made Huizhou, and Dan was made governor.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince assassin established himself, west of the Zhe River in Yang Province was placed under the Director of Retainers. The five commanderies east of the Zhe were made Huizhou, and Dan was made governor.

sentences.zh: 孝武入討，遣甯朔將軍顧彬之受誕節度，誕遣參軍劉季之舉兵與彬之並。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to punish Shao, he sent General of Pacifying the North Gu Binzhi to accept Dan's command; Dan sent Attendant Liu Jizhi to raise troops and join Binzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to punish Shao, he sent General of Pacifying the North Gu Binzhi to accept Dan's command. Dan sent Attendant Liu Jizhi to raise troops and join Binzhi.

sentences.zh: 遇劭將華欽、庾遵于曲阿之奔牛塘，大敗之。

translations.literal: They met Shao's generals Hua Qin and Yu Zun at Benniu Pond in Qu'e and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: They met Shao's generals Hua Qin and Yu Zun at Benniu Pond in Qu'e and routed them.

sentences.zh: 事平，以誕為荊州刺史，加都督、衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled Dan was made Governor of Jingzhou, with added overall command, General of the Guard, and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled Dan was made governor of Jingzhou, with added overall command, General of the Guard, and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 誕以位號正與浚同，惡之，請求回改，乃進號驃騎將軍，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Dan resented that his rank and title were exactly the same as Jun's and requested change; he was therefore promoted General of Agile Cavalry, with twenty ceremonial swords added.
translations.idiomatic: Dan resented that his rank and title were exactly the same as Jun's and requested change. He was therefore promoted General of Agile Cavalry, with twenty ceremonial swords added.

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣不肯就征，以誕為侍中、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史，開府如故。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan refused to accept summons; Dan was made Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Yangzhou, with office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao refused to accept summons. Dan was made Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and governor of Yangzhou, with office as before.

sentences.zh: 改封竟陵王。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prince of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 誕性恭和，得士庶之心，頗有勇略。

translations.literal: Dan was by nature respectful and harmonious and won the hearts of gentry and commoners; he had considerable courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was by nature respectful and harmonious and won the hearts of gentry and commoners. He had considerable courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 明年義宣反，有荊、江、兗、豫四州之力，勢震天下。

translations.literal: The next year Yixuan rebelled with the strength of Jing, Jiang, Yan, and Yu provinces; his momentum shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yixuan rebelled with the strength of Jing, Jiang, Yan, and Yu provinces. His momentum shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 上即位日淺，朝野大懼。

translations.literal: The Emperor had recently taken the throne; court and countryside were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had recently taken the throne. Court and countryside were greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 上欲奉乘輿法物以迎義宣，誕固執不可，曰：「奈何持此座與人。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to carry the imperial regalia to welcome Yixuan; Dan firmly held it impossible and said: "How can you hold this seat and give it to another?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to carry the imperial regalia to welcome Yixuan. Dan firmly held it impossible and said, "How can you hold this seat and give it to another?"

sentences.zh: 」帝加誕節，仗士五十人出入六門。

translations.literal: The Emperor added Dan's credentials; fifty armed men attended his passage through the six gates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added Dan's credentials. Fifty armed men attended his passage through the six gates.

sentences.zh: 上流平定，誕之力也。

translations.literal: Pacifying the upper Yangzi was Dan's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the upper Yangzi was Dan's achievement.

sentences.zh: 誕初討元凶，豫同舉兵，有奔牛之捷，至是又有殊勳。

translations.literal: Dan at first punished the crown prince assassin and jointly raised troops, had the victory at Benniu — and now again had extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Dan at first punished the crown prince assassin and jointly raised troops, had the victory at Benniu — and now again had extraordinary merit.

sentences.zh: 上性多猜，頗相疑憚。

translations.literal: The Emperor by nature was much suspicious and quite feared and dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature was much suspicious and quite feared and dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 而誕造立第舍，窮極工巧，園池之美，冠于一時。

translations.literal: Yet Dan built residences to the utmost of craft and ingenuity; the beauty of gardens and ponds surpassed all of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dan built residences to the utmost of craft and ingenuity. The beauty of gardens and ponds surpassed all of the time.

sentences.zh: 多聚材力之士實之。

translations.literal: He gathered many men of material strength to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered many men of material strength to fill them.

sentences.zh: 第內精甲利器，莫非上品。

translations.literal: Within the residence fine armor and sharp weapons were none that were not top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Within the residence fine armor and sharp weapons were none that were not top grade.

sentences.zh: 上意愈不平。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind grew ever more displeased.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，以司空太子太傅出為都督南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he was sent out as overall commander and Governor of South Xu Province, Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2 he was sent out as overall commander and governor of South Xu Province, Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 上以京口去都密邇，猶疑之。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Jingkou was close and dense to the capital still suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor because Jingkou was close and dense to the capital still suspected him.

sentences.zh: 大明元年秋，又出為南兗州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Daming he was again sent out as Governor of South Yan Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Daming 1 he was again sent out as governor of South Yan Province, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 誕知見猜，亦潛為之備。

translations.literal: Dan knew he was suspected and also secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Dan knew he was suspected and also secretly made preparations.

sentences.zh: 至廣陵，因魏侵邊，修城隍，聚糧練甲。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangling, because Wei invaded the border he repaired walls and moats, gathered grain, and drilled armor.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guangling, because Wei invaded the border he repaired walls and moats, gathered grain, and drilled armor.

sentences.zh: 嫌隙既著，道路常雲誕反。

translations.literal: Suspicion and rift already clear, on the roads people constantly said Dan was rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion and rift already clear, on the roads people constantly said Dan was rebelling.

sentences.zh: 三年，建康人陳文紹訴父饒為誕府史，恒使入山圖畫道路，不聽歸家。

translations.literal: In the third year Chen Wenshao of Jiankang accused his father Rao, a clerk in Dan's household, of constantly being sent into the mountains to map roads and not being allowed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Chen Wenshao of Jiankang accused his father Rao, a clerk in Dan's household, of constantly being sent into the mountains to map roads and not being allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 誕大怒，使人殺饒。

translations.literal: Dan was greatly angered and sent men to kill Rao.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was greatly angered and sent men to kill Rao.

sentences.zh: 吳郡人劉成又訴稱息道龍伏事誕，見誕在石頭城內修乘輿法物，習唱警蹕，向伴侶言之。

translations.literal: Liu Cheng of Wu commandery also accused, saying his son Daolong secretly served Dan, saw Dan within Stone City repairing imperial regalia, practiced shouting the imperial guard, and told his companions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cheng of Wu commandery also accused, saying his son Daolong secretly served Dan, saw Dan within Stone City repairing imperial regalia, practiced shouting the imperial guard, and told his companions.

sentences.zh: 誕知，密捕殺道龍。

translations.literal: Dan learned of it and secretly seized and killed Daolong.
translations.idiomatic: Dan learned of it and secretly seized and killed Daolong.

sentences.zh: 豫章人陳談之又上書稱弟詠之在誕左右，見誕與左右莊慶、傅元禮等潛圖奸逆，常疏陛下年紀姓諱，往巫鄭師憐家咒詛。

translations.literal: Chen Tanzhi of Yuzhang also submitted a memorial saying his younger brother Yongzhi was at Dan's side, saw Dan with attendants Zhuang Qing, Fu Yuanli, and others secretly plotting treachery, constantly listing the Emperor's age and tabooed name, going to the shaman Zheng Shilian's home to curse.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tanzhi of Yuzhang also submitted a memorial saying his younger brother Yongzhi was at Dan's side, saw Dan with attendants Zhuang Qing, Fu Yuanli, and others secretly plotting treachery, constantly listing the emperor's age and tabooed name, going to the shaman Zheng Shilian's home to curse.

sentences.zh: 詠之與建康右尉黃達往來，誕疑其宣漏，誣以罪被殺。

translations.literal: Yongzhi had dealings with Right Commandant of Jiankang Huang Da; Dan suspected he leaked and falsely charged him with crime and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi had dealings with Right Commandant of Jiankang Huang Da. Dan suspected he leaked and falsely charged him with crime and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，上使有司奏誕罪惡，宜絕屬籍，削爵土，收付法獄。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month the Emperor had the relevant office memorialize Dan's crimes and wickedness — he should be cut from the clan register, stripped of rank and fief, and taken to the law prison.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fourth month the emperor had the relevant office memorialize Dan's crimes and wickedness — he should be cut from the clan register, stripped of rank and fief, and taken to the law prison.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 有司又固請，乃貶爵為侯，遣令之國。

translations.literal: The relevant office again firmly requested; he was then demoted in rank to marquis and ordered to go to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office again firmly requested. He was then demoted in rank to marquis and ordered to go to his fief.

sentences.zh: 上將謀誕，以義興太守垣閬為兗州刺史，配以羽林禁兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to plot against Dan and made Yuan Lang of Yixing Governor of Yan Province, assigning Feathered Forest forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to plot against Dan and made Yuan Lang of Yixing governor of Yan Province, assigning Feathered Forest forbidden troops.

sentences.zh: 遣給事中戴明寶隨閬襲誕，使閬以之鎮為名。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Cadet Dai Mingbao to follow Lang in attacking Dan, having Lang use going to his post as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Cadet Dai Mingbao to follow Lang in attacking Dan, having Lang use going to his post as pretext.

sentences.zh: 閬至廣陵，誕未悟也。

translations.literal: Lang reached Guangling; Dan had not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: Lang reached Guangling. Dan had not yet understood.

sentences.zh: 明寶夜報誕典簽蔣成使為內應，成以告府舍人許宗之，宗之告誕。

translations.literal: Mingbao by night reported to Dan's registrar Jiang Cheng to act as inner response; Cheng told household officer Xu Zongzhi, and Zongzhi told Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Mingbao by night reported to Dan's registrar Jiang Cheng to act as inner response. Cheng told household officer Xu Zongzhi, and Zongzhi told Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕驚起，召錄事參軍王璵之曰：「我何罪於天，以至此。

translations.literal: Dan started up in alarm and summoned Recorder Wang Yuzhi, saying: "What crime have I against Heaven, to come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan started up in alarm and summoned Recorder Wang Yuzhi, saying, "What crime have I against Heaven, to come to this?"

sentences.zh: 」斬蔣成，勒兵自衛。

translations.literal: He beheaded Jiang Cheng and compelled troops to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Jiang Cheng and compelled troops to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 遣腹心率壯士擊明寶等破之，閬即遇害，明寶逃自海陵界還。

translations.literal: He sent trusted men leading stalwart warriors to attack Mingbao and others and defeat them; Lang was immediately killed, and Mingbao fled back by way of the Hailing border.
translations.idiomatic: He sent trusted men leading stalwart warriors to attack Mingbao and others and defeat them. Lang was immediately killed, and Mingbao fled back by way of the Hailing border.

sentences.zh: 上遣車騎大將軍沈慶之討誕，誕奉表投之城外，自申于國無負，並言帝宮闈之醜。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi to punish Dan; Dan submitted a memorial thrown outside the wall, declaring himself not unfaithful to the state and also speaking of the ugliness within the imperial palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi to punish Dan. Dan submitted a memorial thrown outside the wall, declaring himself not unfaithful to the state and also speaking of the ugliness within the imperial palace.

sentences.zh: 孝武忿誕深切，凡誕左右腹心同籍期親並誅之，死者千數。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu hated Dan deeply; all Dan's trusted inner men of the same register and near kin were executed — the dead numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu hated Dan deeply. All Dan's trusted inner men of the same register and near kin were executed — the dead numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 車駕出頓宣武堂，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Xuanwu Hall; within and without strict guard was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage halted at Xuanwu Hall. Within and without strict guard was ordered.

sentences.zh: 誕見眾軍大集，欲棄城北走，行十餘里，眾並不欲去，請誕乃還城。

translations.literal: Dan, seeing the mass of armies gathered, wished to abandon the city and flee north; after going more than ten li the host all did not wish to leave and begged Dan — he then returned to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, seeing the mass of armies gathered, wished to abandon the city and flee north. After going more than ten li the host all did not wish to leave and begged Dan — he then returned to the city.

sentences.zh: 五月十九日夜，有流星長十餘丈從西北來墜城內，是謂天狗。

translations.literal: On the night of the nineteenth day of the fifth month a meteor more than ten zhang long came from the northwest and fell within the city — this is called the Celestial Dog.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the nineteenth day of the fifth month a meteor more than ten zhang long came from the northwest and fell within the city — this is called the Celestial Dog.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天狗所墜，下有伏屍流血。

translations.literal: The prognostication says: "Where the Celestial Dog falls, below there are hidden corpses and flowing blood."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication says, "Where the Celestial Dog falls, below there are hidden corpses and flowing blood."

sentences.zh: 」廣陵城舊不開南門，云：「開南門者不利其主」。

translations.literal: The old Guangling city did not open the south gate; they said: "Opening the south gate is unfavorable to its lord."
translations.idiomatic: The old Guangling city did not open the south gate. They said, "Opening the south gate is unfavorable to its lord."

sentences.zh: 誕乃開焉。

translations.literal: Dan then opened it.
translations.idiomatic: Dan then opened it.

sentences.zh: 彭城邵領宗在城內陰結死士欲襲誕，先欲布誠于慶之，乃說誕求為間構，見許。

translations.literal: Shao Lingzong of Pengcheng within the city secretly joined death-loyal men wishing to strike Dan; he first wished to show sincerity to Qingzhi and therefore urged Dan to request to act as agent — permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Lingzong of Pengcheng within the city secretly joined death-loyal men wishing to strike Dan. He first wished to show sincerity to Qingzhi and therefore urged Dan to request to act as agent — permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 領宗既出致誠畢，復還城內。

translations.literal: Lingzong having gone out and shown sincerity completely, returned again within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzong having gone out and shown sincerity completely, returned again within the city.

sentences.zh: 事泄，誕鞭二百，考問不伏，遂支解之。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Dan whipped him two hundred strokes, interrogated under torture but he would not confess, and therefore dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: The affair leaked. Dan whipped him two hundred strokes, interrogated under torture but he would not confess, and therefore dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 上遣送章二紐：其一曰：「竟陵縣開國侯，食邑千戶」。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent two seals: the first said "Marquis of Jingling county, fief of one thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent two seals. The first said, "Marquis of Jingling county, fief of one thousand households."

sentences.zh: 募賞禽誕。

translations.literal: Reward for capturing Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Reward for capturing Dan.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：「建興縣開國男，食邑三百戶」。

translations.literal: The second said "Baron of Jianxing county, fief of three hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: The second said, "Baron of Jianxing county, fief of three hundred households."

sentences.zh: 募賞先登。

translations.literal: Reward for first scaling the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Reward for first scaling the wall.

sentences.zh: 若克外城舉一烽，克內城舉二烽，禽誕舉三烽。

translations.literal: If the outer city was taken one beacon was raised; if the inner city two; if Dan was captured three.
translations.idiomatic: If the outer city was taken one beacon was raised. If the inner city two. If Dan was captured three.

sentences.zh: 七月二日，慶之進軍，克其外城，乘勝又克小城。

translations.literal: On the second day of the seventh month Qingzhi advanced the army and took the outer city; exploiting victory he also took the small city.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the seventh month Qingzhi advanced the army and took the outer city. Exploiting victory he also took the small city.

sentences.zh: 誕聞軍入，走趣後園墜水，引出殺之，傳首建鄴，因葬廣陵，貶姓留氏。

translations.literal: Dan, hearing troops had entered, fled to the rear garden and fell into water; pulled out he was killed; his head was sent to Jiankang; he was buried at Guangling and demoted in surname to Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, hearing troops had entered, fled to the rear garden and fell into water. Pulled out he was killed. His head was sent to Jiankang. He was buried at Guangling and demoted in surname to Liu.

sentences.zh: 帝命城中無大小悉斬，慶之執諫，自五尺以下全之，於是同黨悉伏誅。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that within the city none great or small be spared execution; Qingzhi held and remonstrated — from five chi downward all were spared — and therefore fellow conspirators were all executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that within the city none great or small be spared execution. Qingzhi held and remonstrated — from five chi downward all were spared — and therefore fellow conspirators were all executed by law.

sentences.zh: 城內女口為軍賞，男丁殺為京觀，死者尚數千人，每風晨雨夜有號哭之聲。

translations.literal: Women within the city were taken as army reward; male adults were killed to make a victory mound — the dead still numbered in the thousands; every windy dawn and rainy night there were sounds of wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Women within the city were taken as army reward. Male adults were killed to make a victory mound — the dead still numbered in the thousands. Every windy dawn and rainy night there were sounds of wailing.

sentences.zh: 誕母殷、妻徐並自殺。

translations.literal: Dan's mother Yin and wife Xu both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's mother Yin and wife Xu both killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 追贈殷長寧園淑妃。

translations.literal: Yin was posthumously granted Consort Shu of Changning Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was posthumously granted Consort Shu of Changning Garden.

sentences.zh: 初，誕為南徐州刺史，在京口，夜大風飛落屋瓦，城門鹿床倒覆，誕心惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Dan was Governor of South Xu Province at Jingkou, one night great wind blew down roof tiles; the city gate deer-bed overturned — Dan's heart was ill-disposed toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Dan was governor of South Xu Province at Jingkou, one night great wind blew down roof tiles. The city gate deer-bed overturned — Dan's heart was ill-disposed toward it.

sentences.zh: 及遷鎮廣陵，將入城，沖風暴起，揚塵，晝晦。

translations.literal: When he moved to garrison Guangling and was about to enter the city, a rushing wind suddenly rose and raised dust; day was dim.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved to garrison Guangling and was about to enter the city, a rushing wind suddenly rose and raised dust. Day was dim.

sentences.zh: 又嘗中夜閑坐，有赤光照室，見者莫不駭愕。

translations.literal: He also once sat idle in the middle of the night; red light illuminated the room — all who saw were startled.
translations.idiomatic: He also once sat idle in the middle of the night. Red light illuminated the room — all who saw were startled.

sentences.zh: 誕左右侍直，眠中夢人告之曰：「官鬚髮為矟毦。

translations.literal: Dan's attendants on duty in sleep dreamed a man told them: "Your lord's hair and beard will become spear-bristle."
translations.idiomatic: Dan's attendants on duty in sleep dreamed a man told them, "Your lord's hair and beard will become spear-bristle."

sentences.zh: 」既覺已失髻矣，如此者數十人。

translations.literal: When they awoke the topknot was already lost — thus for several dozen men.
translations.idiomatic: When they awoke the topknot was already lost — thus for several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 誕甚怪懼。

translations.literal: Dan was very strange and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was very strange and afraid.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，發人築廣陵城，誕循行，有人幹輿，揚聲大罵曰：「大兵尋至，何以辛苦百姓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming men were sent to build the Guangling wall; Dan made the rounds; someone in a dry cart shouted curses loudly: "Great armies will soon arrive — why toil the common people?"
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 2 men were sent to build the Guangling wall. Dan made the rounds. Someone in a dry cart shouted curses loudly, "Great armies will soon arrive — why toil the common people?"

sentences.zh: 」誕使執之，問其本末。

translations.literal: Dan sent men to seize him and asked the whole story.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent men to seize him and asked the whole story.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「姓夷名孫，家在海陵。

translations.literal: He answered: "Surname Yi, given name Sun; home at Hailing."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Surname Yi, given name Sun. Home at Hailing."

sentences.zh: 天公與道佛先議，欲燒除此間人。

translations.literal: "The Lord of Heaven and Dao Buddha first discussed, wishing to burn and remove the people here."
translations.idiomatic: "The Lord of Heaven and Dao Buddha first discussed, wishing to burn and remove the people here."

sentences.zh: 道佛苦諫，強得至今。

translations.literal: "Dao Buddha bitterly remonstrated and by force obtained until today."
translations.idiomatic: "Dao Buddha bitterly remonstrated and by force obtained until today."

sentences.zh: 大禍將至，何不立六慎門。

translations.literal: "Great calamity will soon arrive — why not establish the Six-Caution Gate?"
translations.idiomatic: "Great calamity will soon arrive — why not establish the Six-Caution Gate?"

sentences.zh: 」誕問：「六慎門雲何」？

translations.literal: Dan asked: "What is the Six-Caution Gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan asked, "What is the Six-Caution Gate?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「古有言，禍不過六慎門。

translations.literal: He answered: "Antiquity has a saying — calamity does not pass the Six-Caution Gate."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Antiquity has a saying — calamity does not pass the Six-Caution Gate."

sentences.zh: 」誕以其言狂悖，殺之。

translations.literal: Dan because his words were mad and rebellious killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan because his words were mad and rebellious killed him.

sentences.zh: 又五音士忽狂易見鬼，驚怖啼哭曰：「外軍圍城，城上張白布帆。

translations.literal: Also a five-tone master suddenly went mad and saw ghosts; in fright he wept and said: "Outer armies surround the city; on the walls white cloth sails are spread."
translations.idiomatic: Also a five-tone master suddenly went mad and saw ghosts. In fright he wept and said, "Outer armies surround the city. On the walls white cloth sails are spread."

sentences.zh: 」誕執錄二十餘日乃殺。

translations.literal: Dan seized and held him more than twenty days then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan seized and held him more than twenty days then killed him.

sentences.zh: 城陷之日，雲霧晦冥，白虹臨北門，亙屬城內。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell clouds and mist were dark; a white rainbow lay over the north gate, spanning into the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the city fell clouds and mist were dark. A white rainbow lay over the north gate, spanning into the city.

sentences.zh: 八年，前廢帝即位，義陽王昶為徐州刺史，道經廣陵，至墓盡哀，表請改葬誕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Prince of Yiyang Chang was Governor of Xu Province; passing Guangling he mourned fully at the tomb and memorialized requesting reburial for Dan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, when the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Prince Chang of Yiyang was governor of Xu Province. Passing Guangling he mourned fully at the tomb and memorialized requesting reburial for Dan.

sentences.zh: 詔葬誕及妻子並以庶人禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered burial of Dan and wife and children all by commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered burial of Dan and wife and children all by commoner rites.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始四年，又改葬，祭以少牢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming they were again reburied; sacrifice was by young bullock.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 4 of Emperor Ming they were again reburied. Sacrifice was by young bullock.

sentences.zh: 王璵之，琅邪人，有才局。

translations.literal: Wang Yuzhi was a man of Langya, talented and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuzhi was a man of Langya, talented and capable.

sentences.zh: 其五子悉在建鄴。

translations.literal: His five sons were all in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons were all in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 璵之嘗乘城，慶之縛其五子，示而招之，許以富貴。

translations.literal: Yuzhi once mounted the wall; Qingzhi bound his five sons, displayed them and summoned him, promising wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi once mounted the wall. Qingzhi bound his five sons, displayed them and summoned him, promising wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 璵之曰：「吾受主王厚恩，不可以二心。

translations.literal: Yuzhi said: "I received deep grace from my lord prince — I cannot have two hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi said, "I received deep grace from my lord prince — I cannot have two hearts."

sentences.zh: 三十之年，未獲死所耳，安可以私親誘之。

translations.literal: "Thirty years and I have not yet obtained a place to die — how can I be tempted by private kin?"
translations.idiomatic: "Thirty years and I have not yet obtained a place to die — how can I be tempted by private kin?"

sentences.zh: 」五子號叫于外，呼其父。

translations.literal: The five sons wailed outside, calling their father.
translations.idiomatic: The five sons wailed outside, calling their father.

sentences.zh: 及城平，慶之悉撲殺之。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified Qingzhi beat them all to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was pacified Qingzhi beat them all to death.

sentences.zh: 建平宣簡王宏字休度，文帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xuanjian of Jianping Hong, styled Xiudu, was Emperor Wen's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuanjian of Jianping, Hong, styled Xiudu, was Emperor Wen's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 早喪母。

translations.literal: He lost his mother early.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother early.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年，年十一，封建平王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 21, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 宏少而閑素，篤好文籍，文帝寵愛殊常，為立第於雞籠山，盡山水之美。

translations.literal: Hong from youth was quiet and plain, deeply loved literary works; Emperor Wen favored and loved him exceptionally and built a residence for him at Jilong Mountain with the utmost beauty of mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: Hong from youth was quiet and plain and deeply loved literary works. Emperor Wen favored and loved him exceptionally and built a residence for him at Jilong Mountain with the utmost beauty of mountains and waters.

sentences.zh: 建平國職高他國一階，歷位中護軍，中書令。

translations.literal: The Jianping state staff rank was one step higher than other states; he successively held Central Guard General and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianping state staff rank was one step higher than other states. He successively held Central Guard General and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，孝武入討，劭錄宏殿內，自拔莫由。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Assassin usurped the throne and Emperor Xiaowu entered to punish him, Shao recorded Hong within the hall and he could not escape by himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince assassin usurped the throne and Emperor Xiaowu entered to punish him, Shao recorded Hong within the hall and he could not escape by himself.

sentences.zh: 孝武先嘗以一手板與巨集，巨集遣左右親信周法道齎手板詣孝武。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu had once given Hong a hand-board; Hong sent his close attendant Zhou Fadao to carry the hand-board to Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had once given Hong a hand-board. Hong sent his close attendant Zhou Fadao to carry the hand-board to Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 事平，以為尚書左僕射，使迎太后。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and sent to welcome the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and sent to welcome the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 還加中軍將軍、中書監。

translations.literal: On return he was added Central Army General and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was added Central Army General and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為人謙儉周慎，禮賢接士，明達政事，上甚信仗之。

translations.literal: As a man he was humble, frugal, thorough, and careful, honored the worthy and received gentlemen, clear in governance — the Emperor greatly trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was humble, frugal, thorough, and careful, honored the worthy and received gentlemen, clear in governance — the emperor greatly trusted and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 宏少多病，求解尚書令。

translations.literal: Hong from youth was often ill and requested relief from Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong from youth was often ill and requested relief from Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以本號開府儀同三司，未拜薨。

translations.literal: With his original title and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat he had not yet accepted appointment when he died.
translations.idiomatic: With his original title and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat he had not yet accepted appointment when he died.

sentences.zh: 追贈司徒。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 上痛悼甚至，每朔望出臨靈，自為墓誌銘並誄。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved and mourned extremely; every new moon and full moon he went out to attend the spirit, himself composing the tomb inscription and eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved and mourned extremely. Every new moon and full moon he went out to attend the spirit, himself composing the tomb inscription and eulogy.

sentences.zh: 五年，益諸弟國各千戶，薨者不在其例，唯宏追益。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the younger brothers' states were each increased by one thousand households; the dead were not in the rule — only Hong was posthumously increased.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the younger brothers' states were each increased by one thousand households. The dead were not in the rule — only Hong was posthumously increased.

sentences.zh: 子景素嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingsu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingsu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 景素少有父風，位南徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Jingsu from youth had his father's manner; he held the post Governor of South Xu Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu from youth had his father's manner. He held the post governor of South Xu Province, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範為逆，景素雖纂集兵眾以赴朝廷為名，而陰懷兩端。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guiyang Xiufan rebelled, Jingsu though he gathered troops in the name of rushing to aid the court secretly harbored two minds.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Jingsu though he gathered troops in the name of rushing to aid the court secretly harbored two minds.

sentences.zh: 及事平，進號鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was promoted General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled he was promoted General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 景素好文章書籍，招集才義之士，以收名譽，由是朝野屬意。

translations.literal: Jingsu loved literary works and books, gathered men of talent and righteousness, and thereby collected reputation — hence court and countryside looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu loved literary works and books, gathered men of talent and righteousness, and thereby collected reputation — hence court and countryside looked to him.

sentences.zh: 而後廢帝狂凶失道，內外皆謂景素宜當神器；

translations.literal: Yet the Former Deposed Emperor was mad and brutal and lost the Way; within and without all said Jingsu ought to receive the divine vessel;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Former Deposed Emperor was mad and brutal and lost the Way. Within and without all said Jingsu ought to receive the divine vessel.

sentences.zh: 唯廢帝所生陳氏親戚疾忌之，而楊運長、阮佃夫並明帝舊隸，貪幼主以久其權，慮景素立，不見容於長主，深相忌憚。

translations.literal: only the Former Deposed Emperor's birth-mother Chen clansmen hated and envied this, while Yang Yunchang and Ruan Tianfu were both Emperor Ming's old retainers — greedy for a young sovereign to prolong their power, they feared if Jingsu were established they would not be tolerated by a long-reigning lord and deeply suspected and dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Former Deposed Emperor's birth-mother Chen clansmen hated and envied this, while Yang Yunchang and Ruan Tianfu were both Emperor Ming's old retainers — greedy for a young sovereign to prolong their power, they feared if Jingsu were established they would not be tolerated by a long-reigning lord and deeply suspected and dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年，景素防合將軍王季符恨景素，因奔告之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui, Jingsu's Defense and Combine General Wang Jifu resented Jingsu and therefore fled to report him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 3, Jingsu's Defense and Combine General Wang Jifu resented Jingsu and therefore fled to report him.

sentences.zh: 運長等便欲遣軍討之。

translations.literal: Yunchang and others then wished to send troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang and others then wished to send troops to punish him.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝及衛將軍袁粲以下並保持之，景素亦馳遣世子延齡還都，具自申理。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi and General of the Guard Yuan Can and those below all preserved him; Jingsu also hastily sent his heir Yanling back to the capital to declare himself fully.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi and General of the Guard Yuan Can and those below all preserved him. Jingsu also hastily sent his heir Yanling back to the capital to declare himself fully.

sentences.zh: 運長等乃徙季符于梁州，又奪景素鎮北將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yunchang and others then transferred Jifu to Liang Province and also stripped Jingsu of General Who Pacifies the North and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang and others then transferred Jifu to Liang Province and also stripped Jingsu of General Who Pacifies the North and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自是廢帝狂悖日甚，朝野並屬心景素。

translations.literal: From this the Former Deposed Emperor's madness grew daily; court and countryside both set their hearts on Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Former Deposed Emperor's madness grew daily. Court and countryside both set their hearts on Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 陳氏及運長等彌相猜疑。

translations.literal: The Chen clansmen and Yunchang and others ever more mutually suspected.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen clansmen and Yunchang and others ever more mutually suspected.

sentences.zh: 景素因此稍為自防之計，多以金帛結材力之士。

translations.literal: Jingsu therefore gradually made plans for self-defense, often using gold and silk to bind men of material strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu therefore gradually made plans for self-defense, often using gold and silk to bind men of material strength.

sentences.zh: 時大臣誅夷，孝武諸子孫或殺或廢，無復在朝者。

translations.literal: At the time great ministers were executed and purged; Emperor Xiaowu's sons and grandsons were either killed or deposed — none remained at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time great ministers were executed and purged. Emperor Xiaowu's sons and grandsons were either killed or deposed — none remained at court.

sentences.zh: 且景素在蕃甚得人心，而謗聲日積，深懷憂懼。

translations.literal: Moreover Jingsu at his feudatory greatly won people's hearts, while slanderous voices daily accumulated — he deeply harbored worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jingsu at his feudatory greatly won people's hearts, while slanderous voices daily accumulated — he deeply harbored worry and fear.

sentences.zh: 嘗與故吏劉璡獨處曲台，有鵲集於承塵上，飛鳴相追。

translations.literal: He once was alone with former clerk Liu Lin at Qu Terrace; magpies gathered on the canopy beam, flying and calling in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He once was alone with former clerk Liu Lin at Qu Terrace. Magpies gathered on the canopy beam, flying and calling in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 景素泫然曰：「若斯鳥者，游則參於風煙之上，止則隱于林木之下，饑則啄，渴則飲，形體無累於物，得失不關於心，一何樂哉。

translations.literal: Jingsu said with tears: "Birds like these roam joining the wind and mist above, rest hiding in forest and trees below, hunger then peck, thirst then drink — the body unburdened by things, gain and loss unrelated to the heart — how joyful!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu said with tears, "Birds like these roam joining the wind and mist above, rest hiding in forest and trees below, hunger then peck, thirst then drink — the body unburdened by things, gain and loss unrelated to the heart — how joyful!"

sentences.zh: 」時廢帝單馬獨出，遊走郊野。

translations.literal: At the time the Former Deposed Emperor rode alone out, roaming the suburbs and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Former Deposed Emperor rode alone out, roaming the suburbs and wilds.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍曹欣之等謀候廢帝出行，因聚眾作難，事克，奉景素。

translations.literal: Assistant General Cao Xinzhi and others plotted to wait for the Former Deposed Emperor to go out, then gather troops and make trouble; if successful, they would install Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant General Cao Xinzhi and others plotted to wait for the Former Deposed Emperor to go out, then gather troops and make trouble. If successful, they would install Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 景素每禁之，未欲匆匆舉動。

translations.literal: Jingsu always forbade it and did not wish to act in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu always forbade it and did not wish to act in haste.

sentences.zh: 運長密遣傖人周天賜偽投景素勸為異計，景素知即斬之，送首還台。

translations.literal: Yunchang secretly sent a barbarian Zhou Tiansi falsely to join Jingsu and urge a separate plot; Jingsu knew and immediately beheaded him and sent the head back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang secretly sent a barbarian Zhou Tiansi falsely to join Jingsu and urge a separate plot. Jingsu knew and immediately beheaded him and sent the head back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，羽林監垣祗祖奔景素，言台城已潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year Feathered Forest Supervisor Yuan Zhizu fled to Jingsu, saying the palace city had already collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 4 Feathered Forest Supervisor Yuan Zhizu fled to Jingsu, saying the palace city had already collapsed.

sentences.zh: 景素信之，即舉兵。

translations.literal: Jingsu believed it and immediately raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu believed it and immediately raised troops.

sentences.zh: 運長等常疑景素有異志，即纂嚴。

translations.literal: Yunchang and others had always suspected Jingsu of a separate intent and immediately ordered strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang and others had always suspected Jingsu of a separate intent and immediately ordered strict guard.

sentences.zh: 景素本乏威略，不知所為，竟為台軍破，斬之。

translations.literal: Jingsu by nature lacked prestige and strategy, did not know what to do, and in the end was broken by capital troops and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu by nature lacked prestige and strategy, did not know what to do, and in the end was broken by capital troops and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 即葬京口。

translations.literal: He was immediately buried at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately buried at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 廬江王褘字休秀，文帝第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang Hui, styled Xiuxiu, was Emperor Wen's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Lujiang, styled Xiuxiu, was Emperor Wen's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，年十一，封東海王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 22, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，進位司空。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming he was promoted Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 7 he was promoted Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明帝踐阼，進太尉，封廬江王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was promoted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed Prince of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was promoted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed Prince of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 初，廢帝目褘似驢，上以廢帝之言類，故改封焉。

translations.literal: Earlier the Former Deposed Emperor said Hui looked like a donkey; the Emperor because the Former Deposed Emperor's words were of that kind therefore changed the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Former Deposed Emperor said Hui looked like a donkey. The emperor because the Former Deposed Emperor's words were of that kind therefore changed the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 廢帝既誅群公，彌縱狂惑，常語左右曰：「我即大位來，遂未戒嚴，使人邑邑。

translations.literal: After the Former Deposed Emperor executed the high ministers he ever more indulged madness and delusion; he often told attendants: "Since I took the great throne I have never ordered strict guard — it makes one depressed."
translations.idiomatic: After the Former Deposed Emperor executed the high ministers he ever more indulged madness and delusion. He often told attendants, "Since I took the great throne I have never ordered strict guard — it makes one depressed."

sentences.zh: 」江夏王義恭誅後，昶表求入朝，遣典簽蘧法生銜使。

translations.literal: After Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was executed, Chang memorialized requesting entry to court; he sent registrar Qu Fasheng bearing the mission.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was executed, Chang memorialized requesting entry to court. He sent registrar Qu Fasheng bearing the mission.

sentences.zh: 帝謂法生：「義陽與太宰謀反，我政欲討之，今知求還，甚善。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Fasheng: "Prince of Yiyang and the Grand Preceptor plot rebellion — I am just about to punish them; now knowing he asks to return is very good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Fasheng, "Prince Chang of Yiyang and the Grand Preceptor plot rebellion — I am just about to punish them. Now knowing he asks to return is very good."

sentences.zh: 」又問法生：「義陽謀反，何不啟？

translations.literal: He also asked Fasheng: "Prince of Yiyang plots rebellion — why did you not report?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Fasheng, "Prince Chang of Yiyang plots rebellion — why did you not report?"

sentences.zh: 」法生懼，走還彭城，帝因此北討。

translations.literal: Fasheng was afraid, fled back to Pengcheng, and the Emperor therefore marched north to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng was afraid, fled back to Pengcheng, and the emperor therefore marched north to punish.

sentences.zh: 法生至，昶即起兵，統內諸郡並不受命。

translations.literal: When Fasheng arrived Chang immediately raised troops; all commanderies within his jurisdiction refused orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Fasheng arrived Chang immediately raised troops. All commanderies within his jurisdiction refused orders.

sentences.zh: 昶知事不捷，乃夜開門奔魏，棄母妻，唯攜妾一人，作丈夫服騎馬自隨。

translations.literal: Chang knew the affair would not succeed; he therefore opened the gate by night and fled to Wei, abandoning mother and wife, taking only one concubine, dressed as a man riding horse and following himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chang knew the affair would not succeed. He therefore opened the gate by night and fled to Wei, abandoning mother and wife, taking only one concubine, dressed as a man riding horse and following himself.

sentences.zh: 在道慷慨為斷句曰：「白雲滿鄣來，黃塵半天起。

translations.literal: On the road he composed broken lines in high spirit: "White clouds fill the barrier and come; yellow dust rises to half the sky."
translations.idiomatic: On the road he composed broken lines in high spirit: "White clouds fill the barrier and come; yellow dust rises to half the sky."

sentences.zh: 關山四面絕，故鄉幾千里。

translations.literal: "Passes and mountains cut off on four sides; homeland how many thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: "Passes and mountains cut off on four sides; homeland how many thousand li."

sentences.zh: 」因把姬手南望慟哭，左右莫不哀哽。

translations.literal: He therefore took his concubine's hand, looked south and wailed; attendants none who did not sob choked.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore took his concubine's hand, looked south and wailed. Attendants none who did not sob choked.

sentences.zh: 每節悲慟，遙拜其母。

translations.literal: At each stop he mourned in grief and from afar bowed to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At each stop he mourned in grief and from afar bowed to his mother.

sentences.zh: 武昌王渾字休深，文帝第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuchang Hun, styled Xiushen, was Emperor Wen's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hun of Wuchang, styled Xiushen, was Emperor Wen's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年，年九歲，封汝陰王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, at age nine, he was enfeoffed Prince of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 24, at age nine, he was enfeoffed Prince of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 後徙武昌。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was moved to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 渾少而凶戾，嘗忿左右，拔防身刀斫之。

translations.literal: Hun from youth was fierce and cruel; he once grew angry at attendants and drew his personal blade to hack them.
translations.idiomatic: Hun from youth was fierce and cruel. He once grew angry at attendants and drew his personal blade to hack them.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以為中書令。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Assassin usurped the throne he was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince assassin usurped the throne he was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 山陵夕，裸身露頭往散騎省戲，因彎弓射通直郎周朗中枕，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: On the night of the imperial tomb he went naked with head uncovered to the Palace Cadet office to play, bent bow and shot Direct Attendant Gentleman Zhou Lang in the pillow, taking it as laughter and joy.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the imperial tomb he went naked with head uncovered to the Palace Cadet office to play, bent bow and shot Direct Attendant Gentleman Zhou Lang in the pillow, taking it as laughter and joy.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁，文帝第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, Emperor Wen's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was Emperor Wen's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，年十歲，立為建安王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, at age ten, he was established Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 29, at age ten, he was established Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，累遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe of the Former Deposed Emperor he was successively promoted General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe 1 of the Former Deposed Emperor he was successively promoted General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 時帝狂悖無道，誅害群公，忌憚諸父，並聚之殿內，驅捶陵曳，無復人理。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was mad and brutal and without the Way, executed and harmed the high ministers, dreaded and feared the uncles, gathered them all within the hall, drove, beat, humiliated, and dragged them — no longer human reason.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was mad and brutal and without the Way, executed and harmed the high ministers, dreaded and feared the uncles, gathered them all within the hall, drove, beat, humiliated, and dragged them — no longer human reason.

sentences.zh: 休仁及明帝、山陽王休佑形體並肥壯，帝乃以籠盛稱之，以明帝尤肥，號為豬王。

translations.literal: Xiuren and Emperor Ming and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were all stout in body; the Emperor therefore used cages to weigh them — because Emperor Ming was especially fat, he called him Pig Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren and Emperor Ming and Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang were all stout in body. The emperor therefore used cages to weigh them — because Emperor Ming was especially fat, he called him Pig Prince.

sentences.zh: 號休仁為殺王，休佑為賊王。

translations.literal: He called Xiuren Kill-Prince and Xiuyou Thief-Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He called Xiuren Kill-Prince and Xiuyou Thief-Prince.

sentences.zh: 以三王年長，尤所畏憚，故常錄以自近，不離左右。

translations.literal: Because the three princes were older he especially feared and dreaded them and therefore always kept them recorded near himself, not leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: Because the three princes were older he especially feared and dreaded them and therefore always kept them recorded near himself, not leaving his side.

sentences.zh: 東海王褘凡劣，號之驢王。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Hui was altogether inferior — he called him Donkey-Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Donghai was altogether inferior — he called him Donkey-Prince.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休范、巴陵王休若年少，故並得從容。

translations.literal: Prince of Guiyang Xiufan and Prince Ai of Baling Xiuruo were young and therefore all obtained ease.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiufan of Guiyang and Prince Ai of Baling Xiuruo were young and therefore all obtained ease.

sentences.zh: 嘗以木槽盛飯，內諸雜食，攪令和合，掘地為坑阱，實之以泥水。

translations.literal: He once used a wooden trough to hold rice, put in various foods, stirred to mix together, dug a pit trap in the ground and filled it with mud and water.
translations.idiomatic: He once used a wooden trough to hold rice, put in various foods, stirred to mix together, dug a pit trap in the ground and filled it with mud and water.

sentences.zh: 裸明帝內坑中，以槽食置前，令以口就槽中食之，用為歡笑。

translations.literal: He stripped Emperor Ming naked and put him in the pit, placed the trough food before him, ordered him to eat from the trough with his mouth — taking it as merry laughter.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Emperor Ming naked and put him in the pit, placed the trough food before him, ordered him to eat from the trough with his mouth — taking it as merry laughter.

sentences.zh: 欲害明帝及休仁、休佑，前後以十數。

translations.literal: He wished to harm Emperor Ming and Xiuren and Xiuyou — before and after by the tens.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to harm Emperor Ming and Xiuren and Xiuyou — before and after by the tens.

sentences.zh: 休仁多計數，每以笑調佞諛詶悅之，故得推遷。

translations.literal: Xiuren was much scheming; he always used jest, flattery, and fawning to repay and please him — therefore he obtained promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren was much scheming. He always used jest, flattery, and fawning to repay and please him — therefore he obtained promotion.

sentences.zh: 常於休仁前，使左右淫逼休仁所生楊太妃。

translations.literal: He often before Xiuren had attendants forcibly violate Xiuren's birth-mother Consort Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He often before Xiuren had attendants forcibly violate Xiuren's birth-mother Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 左右並不得已順命，至右衛將軍劉道隆，道隆歡以奉旨，盡諸醜狀。

translations.literal: Attendants all had no choice but to obey — up to Right Guard General Liu Daolong, who Daolong gladly followed the order and exhausted every ugly act.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants all had no choice but to obey — up to Right Guard General Liu Daolong, who gladly followed the order and exhausted every ugly act.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉劉蒙妾孕臨月，帝迎入後宮，冀其生男，欲立為太子。

translations.literal: At the time Court Commandant Liu Meng's concubine was pregnant near term; the Emperor welcomed her into the rear palace, hoping she would bear a son and wishing to establish him crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Court Commandant Liu Meng's concubine was pregnant near term. The emperor welcomed her into the rear palace, hoping she would bear a son and wishing to establish him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘗忤旨，帝怒，乃裸之，縛其手腳，以杖貫手腳內，使擔付太官，即日屠豬。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming once went against the order; the Emperor was angry and stripped him naked, bound hands and feet, ran a staff through hands and feet, had him shouldered and delivered to the Imperial Kitchen — that same day to butcher like a pig.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming once went against the order. The emperor was angry and stripped him naked, bound hands and feet, ran a staff through hands and feet, had him shouldered and delivered to the Imperial Kitchen — that same day to butcher like a pig.

sentences.zh: 休仁笑謂帝曰：「未應死。

translations.literal: Xiuren laughed and told the Emperor: "He should not die yet."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren laughed and told the emperor, "He should not die yet."

sentences.zh: 」帝問其故，休仁曰：「待皇太子生，殺豬取肝肺。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; Xiuren said: "Wait until the crown prince is born, then kill the pig and take liver and lungs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the reason. Xiuren said, "Wait until the crown prince is born, then kill the pig and take liver and lungs."

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，曰：「且付廷尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind eased and he said: "For now deliver him to the Court Commandant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind eased and he said, "For now deliver him to the Court Commandant."

sentences.zh: 」一宿出之。

translations.literal: One night he was released.
translations.idiomatic: One night he was released.

sentences.zh: 帝將南游荊、湘二州，明旦欲殺諸父便發，其夕被殺于華林園。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to travel south to Jing and Xiang provinces; the next morning he wished to kill the uncles then depart — that same evening he was killed in Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to travel south to Jing and Xiang provinces. The next morning he wished to kill the uncles then depart — that same evening he was killed in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 休仁即日便執臣禮於明帝。

translations.literal: Xiuren that same day immediately performed subject rites before Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren that same day immediately performed subject rites before Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 時南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先兄弟被害，猶未殯斂，休仁、休佑同載臨之，開帷歡笑，鼓吹往反，時人咸非焉。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Nanping Jingyou and Prince of Lujiang Jingxian brothers had been killed but not yet encoffined; Xiuren and Xiuyou rode together to attend them, opened the curtain and laughed merrily, music going back and forth — people of the time all condemned it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Jingyou of Nanping and Prince Jingxian of Lujiang brothers had been killed but not yet encoffined. Xiuren and Xiuyou rode together to attend them, opened the curtain and laughed merrily, music going back and forth — people of the time all condemned it.

sentences.zh: 明帝以休仁為侍中、司徒、尚書令、揚州刺史，給三望車。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made Xiuren Palace Attendant, Grand Minister of Works, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yangzhou, giving three imperial-view carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming made Xiuren Palace Attendant, Grand Minister of Works, director of the Masters of Writing, and governor of Yangzhou, giving three imperial-view carriages.

sentences.zh: 時劉道隆為護軍，休仁求解職，曰：「臣不得與此人同朝。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Daolong was General of the Guard; Xiuren requested relief from office saying: "I cannot be at court with this man."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Daolong was General of the Guard. Xiuren requested relief from office saying, "I cannot be at court with this man."

sentences.zh: 」上乃賜道隆死。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore granted Daolong death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore granted Daolong death.

sentences.zh: 尋諸方逆命，休仁都督征討諸軍事，增班劍為三十人，出據獸檻，進赭圻。

translations.literal: Shortly rebellions arose in all directions; Xiuren was made overall commander of punitive campaigns, with ceremonial swords increased to thirty; he went out to hold Beast Cage and advanced to Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly rebellions arose in all directions. Xiuren was made overall commander of punitive campaigns, with ceremonial swords increased to thirty. He went out to hold Beast Cage and advanced to Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 尋領太子太傅，總統諸軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he held Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and commanded all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he held Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and commanded all armies.

sentences.zh: 中流平定，休仁之力也。

translations.literal: Pacifying the middle Yangzi was Xiuren's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the middle Yangzi was Xiuren's achievement.

sentences.zh: 明帝初與蘇侯神結為兄弟，以祈福助。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming at first with Lord Su formed brotherhood to seek blessing and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming at first with Lord Su formed brotherhood to seek blessing and aid.

sentences.zh: 及事平，與休仁書曰：「此段殊得蘇兄神力。」

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he wrote to Xiuren: "This stretch truly obtained Elder Brother Su's divine power."
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled he wrote to Xiuren, "This stretch truly obtained Elder Brother Su's divine power."

sentences.zh: 休仁年與明帝相亞，俱好文籍，素相愛。

translations.literal: Xiuren's age was close to Emperor Ming's; both loved literary works and from of old loved each other.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren's age was close to Emperor Ming's. Both loved literary works and from of old loved each other.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝世，同經艱危，明帝又資其權譎之力。

translations.literal: In the Former Deposed Emperor's era they together underwent hardship and peril; Emperor Ming also relied on his crafty scheming power.
translations.idiomatic: In the Former Deposed Emperor's era they together underwent hardship and peril. Emperor Ming also relied on his crafty scheming power.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，四方逆命，休仁親當矢石，大勳克建，任總百揆，親寄甚隆，四方輻湊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, rebellions arose in all directions; Xiuren personally faced arrows and stones, built great merit, held the hundred offices, and received intimate trust very grand — all directions converged like wheel spokes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi, rebellions arose in all directions. Xiuren personally faced arrows and stones, built great merit, held the hundred offices, and received intimate trust very grand — all directions converged like wheel spokes.

sentences.zh: 上甚不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was very displeased.

sentences.zh: 休仁悟其旨，表解揚州，見許。

translations.literal: Xiuren understood his intent and memorialized to relinquish Yangzhou — permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren understood his intent and memorialized to relinquish Yangzhou — permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 進位太尉，領司徒，固讓。

translations.literal: He was promoted Grand Marshal and held Grand Minister of Works — he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Grand Marshal and held Grand Minister of Works — he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又加漆輪車，劍履升殿。

translations.literal: Lacquered wheel carriage was also added, with sword and shoes ascending the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lacquered wheel carriage was also added, with sword and shoes ascending the hall.

sentences.zh: 受漆輪車，固辭劍履。

translations.literal: He accepted the lacquered wheel carriage and firmly declined sword and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the lacquered wheel carriage and firmly declined sword and shoes.

sentences.zh: 明帝末年多忌，休仁轉不自安。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's later years he was much suspicious; Xiuren turned ever less secure.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's later years he was much suspicious. Xiuren turned ever less secure.

sentences.zh: 及殺晉平王休佑，其年上疾篤，與楊運長為身後計。

translations.literal: When Prince Ci of Jinping Xiuyou was killed, that year the Emperor's illness was grave and he with Yang Yunchang made plans for after death.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ci of Jinping Xiuyou was killed, that year the emperor's illness was grave and he with Yang Yunchang made plans for after death.

sentences.zh: 運長等又慮帝晏駕後，休仁一旦居周公之地，其輩不得執權，彌贊成上使害諸王。

translations.literal: Yunchang and others also feared that after the Emperor's death Xiuren might one day occupy the Duke of Zhou's place — their faction would not hold power — and ever more praised and accomplished the Emperor's harming the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang and others also feared that after the emperor's death Xiuren might one day occupy the Duke of Zhou's place — their faction would not hold power — and ever more praised and accomplished the emperor's harming the princes.

sentences.zh: 及上疾暴甚，內外皆屬意休仁。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness suddenly worsened, within and without all set their hearts on Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness suddenly worsened, within and without all set their hearts on Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 主書以下皆往東府詣休仁所親信，豫自結納。

translations.literal: Chief clerks and below all went to the Eastern Headquarters to visit Xiuren's trusted men and beforehand joined themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks and below all went to the Eastern Headquarters to visit Xiuren's trusted men and beforehand joined themselves.

sentences.zh: 其或直不得出者皆懼。

translations.literal: Those who could not go out on duty were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not go out on duty were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 上與運長等定謀，召休仁入宿尚書下省，其夜遣人齎藥賜休仁死，休仁對使者罵曰：「上有天下，誰之功也。

translations.literal: The Emperor with Yunchang and others fixed the plot, summoned Xiuren to lodge overnight in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing; that night sent men bearing medicine to grant Xiuren death; Xiuren cursed the envoy: "The realm above — whose achievement was it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor with Yunchang and others fixed the plot, summoned Xiuren to lodge overnight in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing. That night sent men bearing medicine to grant Xiuren death. Xiuren cursed the envoy, "The realm above — whose achievement was it?"

sentences.zh: 孝武以誅子孫而至於滅，令復遵覆車，枉殺兄弟，奈何忠臣抱此冤濫！

translations.literal: "Emperor Xiaowu reached extinction by executing sons and grandsons — now again following the overturned cart, wrongly killing brothers — how can loyal ministers bear this wrongful flood!"
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Xiaowu reached extinction by executing sons and grandsons — now again following the overturned cart, wrongly killing brothers — how can loyal ministers bear this wrongful flood!"

sentences.zh: 我大宋之業，其能久乎。

translations.literal: "Can the great enterprise of our Great Song long endure?"
translations.idiomatic: "Can the great enterprise of our Great Song long endure?"

sentences.zh: 」上疾久，慮人情同異，自力乘輿出端門，休仁死後乃入。

translations.literal: The Emperor's illness was long; he feared people's hearts would differ and alike; by force he rode the carriage out End Gate — only after Xiuren's death did he enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness was long. He feared people's hearts would differ and alike. By force he rode the carriage out End Gate — only after Xiuren's death did he enter.

sentences.zh: 詔稱其自殺，宥其二子，並全封爵。

translations.literal: An edict said he had killed himself, pardoned his two sons, and fully preserved enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said he had killed himself, pardoned his two sons, and fully preserved enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 有司奏請降休仁為庶人，絕屬籍，兒息悉徙遠郡。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialize requesting demotion of Xiuren to commoner, cut from clan register, sons and heirs all exiled to distant commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialize requesting demotion of Xiuren to commoner, cut from clan register, sons and heirs all exiled to distant commanderies.

sentences.zh: 詔休仁特降為始安縣王，並停子伯融等流徙，聽襲封爵。

translations.literal: An edict specially demoted Xiuren to Prince of Shi'an county and stopped exile of his son Borong and others, permitting succession to enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially demoted Xiuren to Prince of Shi'an county and stopped exile of his son Borong and others, permitting succession to enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 及帝疾甚，見休仁為祟，叫曰：「司徒小寬我。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness was grave he saw Xiuren as an apparition and cried: "Grand Minister of Works, spare me a little."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness was grave he saw Xiuren as an apparition and cried, "Grand Minister of Works, spare me a little."

sentences.zh: 」尋崩。

translations.literal: Shortly he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he died.

sentences.zh: 伯融，妃殷氏所生。

translations.literal: Borong — Consort Yin bore him.
translations.idiomatic: Borong — Consort Yin bore him.

sentences.zh: 殷氏，吳興太守沖女也。

translations.literal: Lady Yin was daughter of Governor of Wuxing Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin was daughter of Governor of Wuxing Chong.

sentences.zh: 范陽祖翻有醫術，姿貌又美，殷氏有疾，翻入視脈，悅之，遂與奸。

translations.literal: Zu Fan of Fanyang had medical skill; his appearance was also beautiful; Lady Yin had illness — Fan entered to feel the pulse, was pleased with her, and therefore had illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Fan of Fanyang had medical skill and his appearance was also beautiful. Lady Yin had illness — Fan entered to feel the pulse, was pleased with her, and therefore had illicit relations.

sentences.zh: 事泄，遣還家賜死。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked he was sent home and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair leaked he was sent home and granted death.

sentences.zh: 晉平刺王休佑，文帝第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Ci of Jinping Xiuyou, Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ci of Jinping, Xiuyou, was Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，年十一，封山陽王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，以山陽荒弊，改封晉平王，位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, because Shanyang was wasted and impoverished he was changed to Prince of Jinping, holding General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, because Shanyang was wasted and impoverished he was changed to Prince of Jinping, holding General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat, and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 休佑素無才能，強梁自用。

translations.literal: Xiuyou by nature had no talent and was overbearing and self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou by nature had no talent and was overbearing and self-willed.

sentences.zh: 大明之世，不得自專，至是貪淫好財色，在荊州多營財貨。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he could not act on his own; reaching this time he was greedy, lecherous, and fond of wealth and beauty; in Jingzhou he greatly amassed goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era he could not act on his own. Reaching this time he was greedy, lecherous, and fond of wealth and beauty. In Jingzhou he greatly amassed goods.

sentences.zh: 以短錢一百賦人，田登就求白米一斛，米粒皆令徹白；

translations.literal: With short cash of one hundred he assessed the people; when fields ripened he demanded white rice one hu, every grain required thoroughly white;
translations.idiomatic: With short cash of one hundred he assessed the people. When fields ripened he demanded white rice one hu, every grain required thoroughly white.

sentences.zh: 若碎折者悉不受。

translations.literal: if broken or crushed none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: If broken or crushed none was accepted.

sentences.zh: 人間糴此米一斗一百。

translations.literal: Among the people this rice sold for one hundred cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people this rice sold for one hundred cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 至時又不受米，評米責錢，凡諸求利皆如此。

translations.literal: When due he again would not accept rice, assessed rice and charged cash — all seeking profit was thus.
translations.idiomatic: When due he again would not accept rice, assessed rice and charged cash — all seeking profit was thus.

sentences.zh: 百姓嗷然，不復堪命。

translations.literal: The common people clamored and could no longer bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The common people clamored and could no longer bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 徵為南徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Governor of South Xu Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as governor of South Xu Province, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 上以休佑貪虐，不可蒞人，留之都下，遣上佐行府州事。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Xiuyou was greedy and cruel and could not govern people kept him in the capital and sent senior aides to conduct prefectural and princely affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor because Xiuyou was greedy and cruel and could not govern people kept him in the capital and sent senior aides to conduct prefectural and princely affairs.

sentences.zh: 休佑狠戾，前後忤上非一。

translations.literal: Xiuyou was fierce and cruel; before and after he went against the Emperor not once.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou was fierce and cruel. Before and after he went against the emperor not once.

sentences.zh: 在荊州時，左右范景達善彈棋，上召之，休佑留不遣。

translations.literal: When in Jingzhou, his attendant Fan Jingda was skilled at pitch-pot; the Emperor summoned him — Xiuyou kept him and did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: When in Jingzhou, his attendant Fan Jingda was skilled at pitch-pot. The emperor summoned him — Xiuyou kept him and did not send him.

sentences.zh: 上怒詰責之，且慮休佑將來難制，欲方便除之。

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily interrogated and reproached him and also feared Xiuyou would in future be hard to control and wished conveniently to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily interrogated and reproached him and also feared Xiuyou would in future be hard to control and wished conveniently to remove him.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，車駕於岩山射雉，有一雉不肯入場，日暮將反，留休佑射之，令不得雉勿歸。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year the imperial carriage at Yanshan shot pheasants; one pheasant would not enter the field; at dusk about to return he kept Xiuyou to shoot it and ordered that without obtaining the pheasant he must not return.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 7 the imperial carriage at Yanshan shot pheasants. One pheasant would not enter the field. At dusk about to return he kept Xiuyou to shoot it and ordered that without obtaining the pheasant he must not return.

sentences.zh: 休佑時從在黃麾內，左右從者並在部伍後。

translations.literal: Xiuyou at the time followed within the yellow banner; attendants and followers were all behind the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou at the time followed within the yellow banner. Attendants and followers were all behind the ranks.

sentences.zh: 休佑便馳去，上遣左右數人隨之。

translations.literal: Xiuyou then galloped away; the Emperor sent several attendants to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou then galloped away. The emperor sent several attendants to follow.

sentences.zh: 上既還，前驅清道，休佑人從悉散，不復相得。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already returned; the vanguard cleared the road; Xiuyou's followers all scattered and could no longer be found together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already returned. The vanguard cleared the road. Xiuyou's followers all scattered and could no longer be found together.

sentences.zh: 上遣壽寂之等諸壯士追之，日已欲闇，與休佑相及，蹴令墜馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent stalwart men including Shou Jizhi to pursue; the sun was about to set when they caught Xiuyou; they kicked and made him fall from the horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent stalwart men including Shou Jizhi to pursue. The sun was about to set when they caught Xiuyou. They kicked and made him fall from the horse.

sentences.zh: 休佑素勇壯，有氣力，奮拳左右排擊，莫得近。

translations.literal: Xiuyou by nature was brave and stout, with strength; he swung fists left and right beating aside — none could approach.
