translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou by nature was brave and stout, with strength. He swung fists left and right beating aside — none could approach.

sentences.zh: 有一人自後引陰，因頓地，即共拉殺之。

translations.literal: One man from behind pulled his genitals; he therefore fell to the ground — they together dragged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: One man from behind pulled his genitals. He therefore fell to the ground — they together dragged and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遣人馳白上，行唱驃騎落馬，上聞驚曰：「驃騎體大，落馬殊不易。

translations.literal: Men were sent galloping to report the Emperor, proclaiming along the way that the General of Agile Cavalry had fallen from his horse; the Emperor hearing was startled and said: "The General of Agile Cavalry has a large body — falling from a horse is especially not easy."
translations.idiomatic: Men were sent galloping to report the emperor, proclaiming along the way that the General of Agile Cavalry had fallen from his horse. The emperor hearing was startled and said, "The General of Agile Cavalry has a large body — falling from a horse is especially not easy."

sentences.zh: 」即遣御醫上藥相系至，頃之休佑左右人至，久已絕矣。

translations.literal: He immediately sent imperial physicians with medicine in succession; shortly Xiuyou's attendants arrived — long already dead.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent imperial physicians with medicine in succession. Shortly Xiuyou's attendants arrived — long already dead.

sentences.zh: 輿以還第，贈司空。

translations.literal: He was carried in a litter back to the residence; posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried in a litter back to the residence. Posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時巴陵王休若在江陵，其日即馳信報休若曰：「吾與驃騎南山射雉，驃騎馬驚，與直閣夏文秀馬相蹋，文秀墮地，驃騎失控，馬重驚，觸松樹墜地落硎中，時頓悶，故馳報弟。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Ai of Baling Xiuruo was at Jiangling; that same day he galloped a message reporting to Xiuruo: "I with the General of Agile Cavalry shot pheasants at South Mountain; the General of Agile Cavalry's horse was startled, and Direct Attendant Xia Wenxiu's horse trampled it; Wenxiu fell to the ground; the General of Agile Cavalry lost control; the horse was again startled, struck a pine tree and fell into a stone trough; for a time he was stunned — therefore I galloped to report, younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Ai of Baling Xiuruo was at Jiangling. That same day he galloped a message reporting to Xiuruo, "I with the General of Agile Cavalry shot pheasants at South Mountain. The General of Agile Cavalry's horse was startled, and Direct Attendant Xia Wenxiu's horse trampled it. Wenxiu fell to the ground. The General of Agile Cavalry lost control. The horse was again startled, struck a pine tree and fell into a stone trough. For a time he was stunned — therefore I galloped to report, younger brother."

sentences.zh: 」其年五月，追免休佑為庶人，十三子並徙晉平。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month he posthumously stripped Xiuyou to commoner; thirteen sons were all exiled to Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fifth month he posthumously stripped Xiuyou to commoner. Thirteen sons were all exiled to Jinping.

sentences.zh: 明帝尋病，見休佑為祟，使使至晉平撫其諸子。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming soon fell ill and saw Xiuyou as an apparition; he sent envoys to Jinping to comfort his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming soon fell ill and saw Xiuyou as an apparition. He sent envoys to Jinping to comfort his sons.

sentences.zh: 帝尋崩。

translations.literal: The Emperor shortly died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shortly died.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元徽元年，聽諸子還都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui of the Former Deposed Emperor permission was granted for the sons to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 1 of the Former Deposed Emperor permission was granted for the sons to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明三年，稱謀反，並賜死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming of Emperor Shun they were charged with plotting rebellion and all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3 of Emperor Shun they were charged with plotting rebellion and all granted death.

sentences.zh: 海陵王休茂，文帝第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Hailing Xiumao, Emperor Wen's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao of Hailing was Emperor Wen's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，年十一，封海陵王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，為雍州刺史，加都督、北中郎將、甯蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he became Governor of Yong Province, with added overall command, General of the North Center, and Protector Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 2 he became governor of Yong Province, with added overall command, General of the North Center, and Protector Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時司馬庾深之行府州事，休茂性急欲自專，深之及主帥每禁之。

translations.literal: At the time Marshal Yu Shenzhi conducted prefectural and princely affairs; Xiumao was impatient and wished to act on his own — Shenzhi and the commanders always restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Marshal Yu Shenzhi conducted prefectural and princely affairs. Xiumao was impatient and wished to act on his own — Shenzhi and the commanders always restrained him.

sentences.zh: 常懷忿，因左右張伯超至所親愛，多罪過，主帥常加訶責。

translations.literal: He constantly harbored resentment; because attendant Zhang Bochao was one he intimately loved and had many faults, the commanders often added reproach.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly harbored resentment. Because attendant Zhang Bochao was one he intimately loved and had many faults, the commanders often added reproach.

sentences.zh: 伯超懼罪，謂休茂曰：「主帥密疏官罪，欲以啟聞。

translations.literal: Bochao feared punishment and told Xiumao: "The commanders secretly memorialize Your Highness's crimes, wishing to report to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Bochao feared punishment and told Xiumao, "The commanders secretly memorialize Your Highness's crimes, wishing to report to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」休茂曰：「今為何計？

translations.literal: Xiumao said: "What plan now?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao said, "What plan now?"

sentences.zh: 」伯超曰：「唯殺行事及主帥，舉兵自衛，縱不成，不失入虜中為王。

translations.literal: Bochao said: "Only kill the acting officer and commanders, raise troops and defend ourselves — even if unsuccessful, we lose nothing by entering the barbarians to be kings."
translations.idiomatic: Bochao said, "Only kill the acting officer and commanders, raise troops and defend ourselves — even if unsuccessful, we lose nothing by entering the barbarians to be kings."

sentences.zh: 」休茂從之，夜使伯超等殺司馬庾深之，集兵建牙馳檄。

translations.literal: Xiumao followed this; by night he had Bochao and others kill Marshal Yu Shenzhi, gathered troops, raised the standard, and galloped the proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao followed this. By night he had Bochao and others kill Marshal Yu Shenzhi, gathered troops, raised the standard, and galloped the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 休茂出城行營，諮議參軍沈暢之等閉門拒之。

translations.literal: Xiumao went out of the city to conduct camp; Advisory Attendant Shen Changzhi and others closed the gate and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao went out of the city to conduct camp. Advisory Attendant Shen Changzhi and others closed the gate and resisted.

sentences.zh: 城陷，斬暢之。

translations.literal: The city fell; Changzhi was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. Changzhi was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 其日，參軍尹玄度起兵攻休茂，禽之，斬首。

translations.literal: That day Attendant Yin Xuandu raised troops to attack Xiumao, captured him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: That day Attendant Yin Xuandu raised troops to attack Xiumao, captured him, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 母妻皆自殺，同黨悉伏誅。

translations.literal: Mother and wife both killed themselves; fellow conspirators were all executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and wife both killed themselves. Fellow conspirators were all executed by law.

sentences.zh: 有司奏絕休茂屬籍，貶姓為留，不許。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialize cutting Xiumao from the clan register and demoting surname to Liu — not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialize cutting Xiumao from the clan register and demoting surname to Liu — not permitted.

sentences.zh: 即葬襄陽。

translations.literal: He was immediately buried at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately buried at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽哀王休業，文帝第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Poyang Xiuye, Emperor Wen's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of Poyang, Xiuye, was Emperor Wen's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，年十一，封鄱陽王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Poyang; in the third year he died; Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou's second son Shihong succeeded; when deposed the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Poyang. In year 3 he died. Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang's second son Shihong succeeded. When deposed the state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，以山陽王休佑次子士弘嗣，被廢國除。

translations.literal: Prince Chong of Linqing Xiuqian, Emperor Wen's sixteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong of Linqing, Xiuqian, was Emperor Wen's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 臨慶沖王休倩，文帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, at age nine, gravely ill, he was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping — before investiture he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1, at age nine, gravely ill, he was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping — before investiture he died.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，年九歲，疾篤，封東平王，未拜，薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming the twenty-seventh imperial son Zisi was established Prince of Dongping to succeed Xiuqian.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 7 the twenty-seventh imperial son Zisi was established Prince of Dongping to succeed Xiuqian.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，立第二十七皇子子嗣為東平王，紹休倩。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi he returned to his original line — thus ended.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 3 he returned to his original line — thus ended.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年還本，遂絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the fifth imperial son Zhijing was made Prince of Dongping to succeed Xiuqian — before investiture he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 the fifth imperial son Zhijing was made Prince of Dongping to succeed Xiuqian — before investiture he died.

sentences.zh: 六年，以第五皇子智井為東平王，繼休倩，未拜，薨。

translations.literal: That year Xiuqian was posthumously changed to Prince of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xiuqian was posthumously changed to Prince of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 其年，追改休倩為臨慶王。

translations.literal: Xiuqian was loved by Emperor Wen — therefore succession was repeatedly added before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqian was loved by Emperor Wen — therefore succession was repeatedly added before and after.

sentences.zh: 休倩為文帝所愛，故前後屢加紹嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Xinye Yifu, Emperor Wen's seventeenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Xinye, Yifu, was Emperor Wen's seventeenth son.

sentences.zh: 新野懷王夷父，文帝第十七子也。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia; in the fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming enfeoffment and posthumous title were added.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanjia 29. In Taishi 5 of Emperor Ming enfeoffment and posthumous title were added.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年薨，明帝泰始五年，追加封諡。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi went out and halted at Xinting rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi went out and halted at Xinting rampart.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝出次新亭壘。

translations.literal: Affairs arose in haste; court military strength was very weak; when the armory was opened the officers and soldiers took as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs arose in haste. Court military strength was very weak. When the armory was opened the officers and soldiers took as they wished.

sentences.zh: 時事起倉卒，朝廷兵力甚弱，及開武庫，隨將士意取。

translations.literal: Xiufan from Xinlin steps attacked Xinting rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan from Xinlin steps attacked Xinting rampart.

sentences.zh: 休范于新林步上攻新亭壘。

translations.literal: Xiufan from Xinlin steps attacked Xinting rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan from Xinlin steps attacked Xinting rampart.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉黃回乃偽往降，並宣齊高帝意。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Palace Riders Huang Hui then falsely went to surrender and also proclaimed Emperor Gao of Qi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Palace Riders Huang Hui then falsely went to surrender and also proclaimed Emperor Gao of Qi's intent.

sentences.zh: 休範大悅，置之左右。

translations.literal: Xiufan was greatly pleased and placed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan was greatly pleased and placed him at his side.

sentences.zh: 休范壯士李恒、鍾爽進諫不宜親之，休範曰：「不欺人以信。

translations.literal: Xiufan's stalwart Li Heng and Zhong Shuang advanced remonstrance that he should not be intimate with him; Xiufan said: "I do not deceive people — that is trust."
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan's stalwart Li Heng and Zhong Shuang advanced remonstrance that he should not be intimate with him. Xiufan said, "I do not deceive people — that is trust."

sentences.zh: 」時休範日飲醇酒，以二子德宣、德嗣付與齊高帝為質，至即斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiufan daily drank strong wine; he entrusted his two sons Dexuan and Desi to Emperor Gao of Qi as hostages — upon arrival they were immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiufan daily drank strong wine. He entrusted his two sons Dexuan and Desi to Emperor Gao of Qi as hostages — upon arrival they were immediately beheaded.

sentences.zh: 回與越騎校尉張敬兒直前斬休範首持還，左右並散。

translations.literal: Hui with Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Zhang Jinger went straight forward and beheaded Xiufan, holding the head and returning — attendants all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hui with Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Zhang Jinger went straight forward and beheaded Xiufan, holding the head and returning — attendants all scattered.

sentences.zh: 初，休范自新林分遣同黨杜墨蠡、丁文豪等直向朱雀門。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiufan from Xinlin separately sent fellow conspirators Du Molí and Ding Wenhao and others straight toward Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiufan from Xinlin separately sent fellow conspirators Du Molí and Ding Wenhao and others straight toward Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 休範雖死，墨蠡等不知。

translations.literal: Though Xiufan was dead, Molí and others did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiufan was dead, Molí and others did not know.

sentences.zh: 王道隆率羽林兵在朱雀門內，聞賊至，急召劉勉，勉自石頭來赴戰，死之。

translations.literal: Wang Daolong led Feathered Forest troops within Vermilion Bird Gate; hearing bandits had arrived he urgently summoned Liu Mian; Mian came from Stone City to join battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong led Feathered Forest troops within Vermilion Bird Gate. Hearing bandits had arrived he urgently summoned Liu Mian. Mian came from Stone City to join battle and died.

sentences.zh: 墨蠡等乘勝直入朱雀門，道隆為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Molí and others exploited victory and straight entered Vermilion Bird Gate; Daolong was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Molí and others exploited victory and straight entered Vermilion Bird Gate. Daolong was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 墨蠡等唱云：「太尉至」。

translations.literal: Molí and others proclaimed: "The Grand Marshal has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Molí and others proclaimed, "The Grand Marshal has arrived."

sentences.zh: 休范之死也，齊高帝遣隊主陳靈寶齎首還台，逢賊，埋首道側，挺身得達。

translations.literal: When Xiufan died Emperor Gao of Qi sent Company Commander Chen Lingbao bearing the head back to the capital; meeting bandits he buried the head beside the road and by body alone reached.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiufan died Emperor Gao of Qi sent Company Commander Chen Lingbao bearing the head back to the capital. Meeting bandits he buried the head beside the road and by body alone reached.

sentences.zh: 雖唱雲已平，而無以為據，眾愈疑惑。

translations.literal: Though they proclaimed it was already pacified, there was nothing to serve as proof — the host grew ever more doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Though they proclaimed it was already pacified, there was nothing to serve as proof — the host grew ever more doubtful.

sentences.zh: 墨蠡徑至杜姥宅，宮省恇擾，無復固志。

translations.literal: Molí went straight to Old Du's residence; palace offices were alarmed and confused — no longer fixed will.
translations.idiomatic: Molí went straight to Old Du's residence. Palace offices were alarmed and confused — no longer fixed will.

sentences.zh: 撫軍長史褚澄以東府納賊。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army Chu Cheng with the Eastern Headquarters admitted the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army Chu Cheng with the Eastern Headquarters admitted the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊擁安成王據東府，稱休範教曰：「安成王吾子也，勿得侵。

translations.literal: The bandits supported Prince of Ancheng and held the Eastern Headquarters, proclaiming Xiufan's order: "Prince of Ancheng is my son — do not harm."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits supported Prince of Ancheng and held the Eastern Headquarters, proclaiming Xiufan's order, "Prince of Ancheng is my son — do not harm."

sentences.zh: 」賊勢方逼，眾莫能振。

translations.literal: Bandit momentum was just pressing; the host none could rouse.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit momentum was just pressing. The host none could rouse.

sentences.zh: 尋而丁文豪之眾知休範已死，稍欲退散。

translations.literal: Shortly Ding Wenhao's host learned Xiufan was already dead and gradually wished to retreat and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly Ding Wenhao's host learned Xiufan was already dead and gradually wished to retreat and scatter.

sentences.zh: 文豪勇氣殊壯，厲聲曰：「我獨不能定天下邪。

translations.literal: Wenhao's courage was exceptionally stout; he said harshly: "Can I alone not settle the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenhao's courage was exceptionally stout. He said harshly, "Can I alone not settle the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」休範首至，又羽林監陳顯達率所領于杜姥宅破墨蠡等，諸賊一時奔散。

translations.literal: When Xiufan's head arrived, also Feathered Forest Supervisor Chen Xianda led those under his command at Old Du's residence to break Molí and others — all bandits at once fled scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiufan's head arrived, also Feathered Forest Supervisor Chen Xianda led those under his command at Old Du's residence to break Molí and others — all bandits at once fled scattered.

sentences.zh: 斬墨蠡、文豪等。

translations.literal: Molí, Wenhao, and others were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Molí, Wenhao, and others were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王燮自夏口遣軍平尋陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to acting Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was changed to acting governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 四年，改行湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became Governor of Jing Province, with added overall command, Grand General Who Conquers the West, and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became governor of Jing Province, with added overall command, Grand General Who Conquers the West, and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，為荊州刺史，加都督、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince of Jinping Xiuyou was killed and Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was suspected; in the capital false reports said Xiuruo had a prophecy of supreme honor — Emperor Ming because of this speech reported it to him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Prince Xiuyou of Jinping was killed and Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was suspected. In the capital false reports said Xiuruo had a prophecy of supreme honor — Emperor Ming because of this speech reported it to him.

sentences.zh: 七年，晉平王休佑被殺，建安王休仁見疑，都下訛言休若有至貴之表，明帝以此言報之。

translations.literal: Xiuruo was very worried; once with guests filling the seats a strange bird gathered at the corner of the mat, mourned and fell dead to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo was very worried. Once with guests filling the seats a strange bird gathered at the corner of the mat, mourned and fell dead to the ground.

sentences.zh: 休若甚憂，嘗眾賓滿坐，有一異鳥集席隅，哀鳴墜地死。

translations.literal: Also on the audience hall were two great white serpents more than one zhang long, humming with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Also on the audience hall were two great white serpents more than one zhang long, humming with sound.

sentences.zh: 又聽事上有二大白蛇長丈餘，唅唅有聲。

translations.literal: Xiuruo was very ill-disposed toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo was very ill-disposed toward it.

sentences.zh: 休若甚惡之。

translations.literal: He was then summoned as Governor of South Xu Province, with added overall command and Grand General Who Conquers the North, office as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned as governor of South Xu Province, with added overall command and Grand General Who Conquers the North, office as before.

sentences.zh: 會被徵為南徐州刺史，加都督、征北大將軍，開府如故。

translations.literal: Xiuruo's trusted generals and aides all said returning to court would surely bring great calamity; Army Attendant Wang Jingxian of Jingzhao urged holding Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo's trusted generals and aides all said returning to court would surely bring great calamity. Army Attendant Wang Jingxian of Jingzhao urged holding Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 休若腹心將佐咸謂還朝必有大禍，中兵參軍京兆王敬先勸割據荊楚。

translations.literal: Xiuruo seized and held him, galloped envoys to report to Emperor Ming — Jingxian was executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo seized and held him, galloped envoys to report to Emperor Ming — Jingxian was executed for the crime.

sentences.zh: 休若執錄，馳使白明帝，敬先坐誅。

translations.literal: Xiuruo reached Jingkou; the Emperor because Xiuruo was good at harmonizing human sentiment feared he would in future overturn the young sovereign and wished to send men to kill him — feared they would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo reached Jingkou. The emperor because Xiuruo was good at harmonizing human sentiment feared he would in future overturn the young sovereign and wished to send men to kill him — feared they would not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 休若至京口，上以休若善能諧緝物情，慮將來傾幼主，欲遣使殺之，慮不奉詔。

translations.literal: Summoning him to court again feared alarm and shock.
translations.idiomatic: Summoning him to court again feared alarm and shock.

sentences.zh: 征入朝，又恐猜駭。

translations.literal: He falsely appointed him Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely appointed him governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 乃偽授為江州刺史，至，即於第賜死，贈侍中、司空。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he was immediately granted death at his residence; posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he was immediately granted death at his residence. Posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子沖始襲封。

translations.literal: His son Chong at first succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong at first succeeded to the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝二十八男。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu had twenty-eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had twenty-eight sons.

sentences.zh: 文穆皇后生廢帝子業、豫章王子尚。

translations.literal: Empress Wenmu bore the Former Deposed Emperor Ziye and Prince of Yuzhang Zishang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenmu bore the Former Deposed Emperor Ziye and Prince Zishang of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 陳淑媛生晉安王子勳。

translations.literal: Lady Chen bore Prince of Jin'an Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen bore Prince Zixun of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 阮容華生安陸王子綏。

translations.literal: Lady Ruan bore Prince of Anlu Zisui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ruan bore Prince Zisui of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 徐昭容生皇子子深。

translations.literal: Lady Xu bore Imperial Son Zishen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu bore Imperial Son Zishen.

sentences.zh: 何淑儀生松滋侯子房。

translations.literal: Lady He bore Marquis of Songzi Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He bore Marquis Zifang of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 史昭華生臨海王子頊。

translations.literal: Lady Shi bore Prince of Linhai Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi bore Prince Zixiang of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 殷貴妃生始平孝敬王子鸞。

translations.literal: Consort Yin bore Prince Xiaojing of Shiping Ziluan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yin bore Prince Xiaojing of Shiping, Ziluan.

sentences.zh: 次永嘉王子仁與皇子子深同生。

translations.literal: Next Prince of Yongjia Ziren was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zishen.
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Ziren of Yongjia was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zishen.

sentences.zh: 何婕妤生皇子子鳳。

translations.literal: Lady He bore Imperial Son Zifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He bore Imperial Son Zifeng.

sentences.zh: 謝昭容生始安王子真。

translations.literal: Lady Xie bore Prince of Shi'an Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie bore Prince Zizhen of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 江婕妤生皇子子玄。

translations.literal: Lady Jiang bore Imperial Son Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang bore Imperial Son Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 史昭儀生邵陵王子元。

translations.literal: Lady Shi bore Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi bore Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 次齊敬王子羽與始平孝敬王子鸞同生。

translations.literal: Next Prince Jing of Qi Ziyu was born of the same mother as Prince Xiaojing of Shiping Ziluan.
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Jing of Qi, Ziyu, was born of the same mother as Prince Xiaojing of Shiping, Ziluan.

sentences.zh: 江美人生皇子子衡。

translations.literal: Lady Jiang bore Imperial Son Ziheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang bore Imperial Son Ziheng.

sentences.zh: 楊婕妤生淮南王子孟。

translations.literal: Lady Yang bore Prince of Huainan Zimeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang bore Prince Zimeng of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 次皇子子況與皇子子玄同生；

translations.literal: Next Imperial Son Zikuang was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zixuan;
translations.idiomatic: Next Imperial Son Zikuang was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 次南平王子產與永嘉王子仁同生；

translations.literal: next Prince of Nanping Zichan was born of the same mother as Prince of Yongjia Ziren;
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Zichan of Nanping was born of the same mother as Prince Ziren of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 次晉陵孝王子雲、次皇子子文並與始平孝敬王子鸞同生；

translations.literal: next Prince Xiao of Jinling Ziyun, next Imperial Son Ziwen were both born of the same mother as Prince Xiaojing of Shiping Ziluan;
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Xiaojing of Jinling, Ziyun, and next Imperial Son Ziwen were both born of the same mother as Prince Xiaojing of Shiping, Ziluan.

sentences.zh: 次廬陵王子輿與淮南王子孟同生；

translations.literal: next Prince of Luling Ziyu was born of the same mother as Prince of Huainan Zimeng;
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Ziyu of Luling was born of the same mother as Prince Zimeng of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 次南海哀王子師與始平孝敬王子鸞同生；

translations.literal: next Prince Ai of Nanhai Zishi was born of the same mother as Prince Xiaojing of Shiping Ziluan;
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Ai of Nanhai, Zishi, was born of the same mother as Prince Xiaojing of Shiping, Ziluan.

sentences.zh: 次淮陽思王子霄與皇子子玄同生；

translations.literal: next Prince Si of Huaiyang Zixiao was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zixuan;
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Si of Huaiyang, Zixiao, was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 次皇子子雍與始安王子真同生；

translations.literal: next Imperial Son Ziyong was born of the same mother as Prince of Shi'an Zizhen;
translations.idiomatic: Next Imperial Son Ziyong was born of the same mother as Prince Zizhen of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 次皇子子趨與皇子子鳳同生；

translations.literal: Next Imperial Son Ziqu was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zifeng;
translations.idiomatic: Next Imperial Son Ziqu was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Zifeng.

sentences.zh: 次皇子子期與皇子子衡同生；

translations.literal: next Imperial Son Ziqi was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Ziheng;
translations.idiomatic: Next Imperial Son Ziqi was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Ziheng.

sentences.zh: 次東平王子嗣與始安王子真同生。

translations.literal: next Prince of Dongping Zisi was born of the same mother as Prince of Shi'an Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Zisi of Dongping was born of the same mother as Prince Zizhen of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 張容華生皇子子悅。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang bore Imperial Son Ziyue.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang bore Imperial Son Ziyue.

sentences.zh: 安陸王子綏、南平王子產、廬陵王子輿並出繼。

translations.literal: Prince of Anlu Zisui, Prince of Nanping Zichan, and Prince of Luling Ziyu were all given out in adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zisui of Anlu, Prince Zichan of Nanping, and Prince Ziyu of Luling were all given out in adoption.

sentences.zh: 皇子子深、子鳳、子玄、子衡、子況、子文、子雍未封早夭。

translations.literal: Imperial Sons Zishen, Zifeng, Zixuan, Ziheng, Zikuang, and Ziwen were not enfeoffed and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Sons Zishen, Zifeng, Zixuan, Ziheng, Zikuang, and Ziwen were not enfeoffed and died early.

sentences.zh: 子趨、子期、子悅未封，為明帝所殺。

translations.literal: Ziqu, Ziqi, and Ziyue were not enfeoffed and were killed by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqu, Ziqi, and Ziyue were not enfeoffed and were killed by Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 豫章王子尚字孝師，孝武第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Zishang, styled Xiaoshi, was Emperor Xiaowu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, styled Xiaoshi, was Emperor Xiaowu's second son.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，年六歲，封西陽王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian, at age six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 3, at age six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，分浙江西立王畿；

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, west of the Zhe River was established as the King's Domain;
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 3, west of the Zhe River was established as the King's Domain.

sentences.zh: 以浙江東為揚州，以子尚為刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: east of the Zhe was made Yang Province; Zishang was made governor, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Zhe was made Yang Province. Zishang was made governor, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封豫章王，領會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Prince of Yuzhang, holding Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was changed to Prince of Yuzhang, holding governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 七年，進號車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was promoted Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時東土大旱，鄞縣多疇田，孝武使子尚表至鄞縣勸農，又立左學，召生徒，置儒林祭酒一人，學生師敬，位比州中從事。

translations.literal: At the time the eastern land had great drought; Yin county had much fallow field; Emperor Xiaowu had Zishang memorialize arrival at Yin county to encourage agriculture, also established the Left Academy, summoned students, and appointed one Confucian Forest Sacrificer — students and teachers honored him, rank equal to a commandery attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eastern land had great drought and Yin county had much fallow field. Emperor Xiaowu had Zishang memorialize arrival at Yin county to encourage agriculture, also established the Left Academy, summoned students, and appointed one Confucian Forest Sacrificer — students and teachers honored him, rank equal to a commandery attendant.

sentences.zh: 文學祭酒一人，比州西曹。

translations.literal: One Literary Sacrificer, rank equal to the commandery Western Cao.
translations.idiomatic: One Literary Sacrificer, rank equal to the commandery Western Cao.

sentences.zh: 勸學從事二人比祭酒從事。

translations.literal: Two Encourage-Learning Attendants, rank equal to the Sacrificer's attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Two Encourage-Learning Attendants, rank equal to the Sacrificer's attendants.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勳字孝德，孝武第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Zixun, styled Xiaode, was Emperor Xiaowu's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zixun of Jin'an, styled Xiaode, was Emperor Xiaowu's third son.

sentences.zh: 眼患風，不為孝武所愛。

translations.literal: His eyes suffered wind ailment; he was not loved by Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes suffered wind ailment. He was not loved by Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，年五歲，封晉安王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 4, at age five, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 七年，為江州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became Governor of Jiang Province, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he became governor of Jiang Province, with added overall command.

sentences.zh: 八年，改授雍州，未拜而孝武崩，還為江州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was reassigned to Yong Province; before investiture Emperor Xiaowu died — he returned to Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was reassigned to Yong Province. Before investiture Emperor Xiaowu died — he returned to Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 時廢帝狂凶，多所誅害。

translations.literal: At the time the Former Deposed Emperor was mad and brutal and executed many.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Former Deposed Emperor was mad and brutal and executed many.

sentences.zh: 前撫軍諮議參軍何邁謀因帝出為變，迎立子勳。

translations.literal: Former Pacification Army Advisory Attendant He Mai plotted to take advantage of the Emperor going out to make trouble and welcome Zixun to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: Former Pacification Army Advisory Attendant He Mai plotted to take advantage of the emperor going out to make trouble and welcome Zixun to establish him.

sentences.zh: 事泄，帝誅邁，使八座奏子勳與邁通謀，遣左右朱景送藥賜子勳死。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; the Emperor executed Mai and had the Eight Dignitaries memorialize that Zixun with Mai shared conspiracy; he sent attendant Zhu Jing bearing medicine to grant Zixun death.
translations.idiomatic: The affair leaked. The emperor executed Mai and had the Eight Dignitaries memorialize that Zixun with Mai shared conspiracy. He sent attendant Zhu Jing bearing medicine to grant Zixun death.

sentences.zh: 景至盆口，遣報長史鄧琬。

translations.literal: Jing reached Penkou and sent report to Chief Clerk Deng Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reached Penkou and sent report to Chief Clerk Deng Wan.

sentences.zh: 琬等奉子勳起兵，以廢立為名。

translations.literal: Wan and others installed Zixun and raised troops, taking deposition and establishment as their banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and others installed Zixun and raised troops, taking deposition and establishment as their banner.

sentences.zh: 明帝定亂，進子勳車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the disorder he promoted Zixun Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming settled the disorder he promoted Zixun Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 琬等不受命。

translations.literal: Wan and others did not accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and others did not accept the order.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月七日，奉子勳為帝，即偽位於尋陽，年號義嘉，備置百官，四方回應。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi they installed Zixun as emperor; he falsely took the throne at Xunyang, era name Yijia, fully appointing the hundred offices — all directions responded.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the first month of Taishi 2 they installed Zixun as emperor. He falsely took the throne at Xunyang, era name Yijia, fully appointing the hundred offices — all directions responded.

sentences.zh: 是歲四方貢計，並詣尋陽。

translations.literal: That year tribute accounts from all directions all went to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year tribute accounts from all directions all went to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 及軍敗，子勳見殺，時年十一。

translations.literal: When the armies were defeated Zixun was killed — at the time he was eleven.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies were defeated Zixun was killed — at the time he was eleven.

sentences.zh: 即葬尋陽廬山。

translations.literal: He was immediately buried at Lushan, Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately buried at Lushan, Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 始平孝敬王子鸞字孝羽，孝武第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaojing of Shiping Ziluan, styled Xiaoyu, was Emperor Xiaowu's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaojing of Shiping, Ziluan, styled Xiaoyu, was Emperor Xiaowu's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，封襄陽王，尋改封新安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiangyang; shortly changed to Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 4 he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiangyang. Shortly he was changed to Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 五年，為北中郎將、南徐州刺史，領南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was General of the North Center and Governor of South Xu Province, holding Governor of South Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was General of the North Center and governor of South Xu Province, holding governor of South Langye.

sentences.zh: 母殷淑儀寵傾後宮，子鸞愛冠諸子，凡為上眄遇者莫不入子鸞府國。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Yin Shuyi enjoyed favor overturning the rear palace; Ziluan's love topped all sons — whatever the Emperor favored none did not enter Ziluan's princely household.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Yin Shuyi enjoyed favor overturning the rear palace. Ziluan's love topped all sons — whatever the emperor favored none did not enter Ziluan's princely household.

sentences.zh: 為南徐州，又割吳郡屬之。

translations.literal: As Governor of South Xu he also cut off Wu commandery and attached it.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of South Xu he also cut off Wu commandery and attached it.

sentences.zh: 六年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he completed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he completed mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝素疾子鸞有寵，及即位，既誅群臣，乃遣使賜子鸞死，時年十歲。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor from of old resented Ziluan's favor; when he took the throne, having executed the ministers, he sent envoys to grant Ziluan death — at the time he was ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor from of old resented Ziluan's favor. When he took the throne, having executed the ministers, he sent envoys to grant Ziluan death — at the time he was ten.

sentences.zh: 子鸞臨死謂左右曰：「願後身不復生王家。

translations.literal: Ziluan facing death told attendants: "May my later body not again be born in a royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan facing death told attendants, "May my later body not again be born in a royal house."

sentences.zh: 」同生弟妹並死。

translations.literal: Younger brothers and sisters born of the same mother all died.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers and sisters born of the same mother all died.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，改封始平王，以建平王景素子延年嗣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he changed the enfeoffment to Prince of Shiping; Prince of Jianping Jingsu's son Yannian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he changed the enfeoffment to Prince of Shiping. Prince Jingsu of Jianping's son Yannian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 永嘉王子仁字孝和，孝武第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yongjia Ziren, styled Xiaohe, was Emperor Xiaowu's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziren of Yongjia, styled Xiaohe, was Emperor Xiaowu's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，封永嘉王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming he was enfeoffed Prince of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 5 he was enfeoffed Prince of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，以為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was made Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was made governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 帝尋從司徒建安王休仁計，未拜賜死，時年十歲。

translations.literal: The Emperor shortly followed Grand Minister of Works Prince of Jian'an Xiuren's plan — before investiture granted death; at the time he was ten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shortly followed Grand Minister of Works Prince Xiuren of Jian'an's plan — before investiture granted death. At the time he was ten.

sentences.zh: 始安王子真字孝貞，孝武第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shi'an Zizhen, styled Xiaozhen, was Emperor Xiaowu's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zizhen of Shi'an, styled Xiaozhen, was Emperor Xiaowu's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王子元字孝善，孝武第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan, styled Xiaoshan, was Emperor Xiaowu's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling, styled Xiaoshan, was Emperor Xiaowu's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 並被明帝賜死。

translations.literal: Both were granted death by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Both were granted death by Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 淮南王子孟字孝光，孝武第十六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huainan Zimeng, styled Xiaoguang, was Emperor Xiaowu's sixteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zimeng of Huainan, styled Xiaoguang, was Emperor Xiaowu's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 初封淮南王，明帝改封安成王，未拜賜死。

translations.literal: First enfeoffed Prince of Huainan; Emperor Ming changed to Prince of Ancheng — before investiture granted death.
translations.idiomatic: First enfeoffed Prince of Huainan. Emperor Ming changed to Prince of Ancheng — before investiture granted death.

sentences.zh: 晉陵孝王子雲字孝舉，孝武第十九子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Jinling Ziyun, styled Xiaoju, was Emperor Xiaowu's nineteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaojing of Jinling, Ziyun, styled Xiaoju, was Emperor Xiaowu's nineteenth son.

sentences.zh: 大明六年封，未拜而亡。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the sixth year of Daming — before investiture he died.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed in Daming 6 — before investiture he died.

sentences.zh: 南海哀王子師字孝友，孝武第二十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Nanhai Zishi, styled Xiaoyou, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of Nanhai, Zishi, styled Xiaoyou, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-second son.

sentences.zh: 大明七年封，未拜，為前廢帝所害。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the seventh year of Daming — before investiture harmed by the Former Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed in Daming 7 — before investiture harmed by the Former Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位追諡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 淮陽思王子霄字孝雲，孝武第二十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Si of Huaiyang Zixiao, styled Xiaoyun, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Si of Huaiyang, Zixiao, styled Xiaoyun, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-third son.

sentences.zh: 早薨，追加封諡。

translations.literal: Died early; enfeoffment and posthumous title were added afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Died early. Enfeoffment and posthumous title were added afterward.

sentences.zh: 東平王子嗣字孝叔，孝武帝第二十七子也，明帝賜死。

translations.literal: Prince of Dongping Zisi, styled Xiaoshu, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-seventh son — granted death by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zisi of Dongping, styled Xiaoshu, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-seventh son — granted death by Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 武陵王贊字仲敷，小字智隨，明帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Zan, styled Zhongfu, childhood name Zhizui, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zan of Wuling, styled Zhongfu, childhood name Zhizui, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 明帝既誅孝武諸子，詔以智隨奉孝武為子，封武陵郡王。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming having executed Emperor Xiaowu's sons, by edict had Zhizui succeed Emperor Xiaowu as son and enfeoffed Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming having executed Emperor Xiaowu's sons, by edict had Zhizui succeed Emperor Xiaowu as son and enfeoffed Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明二年薨，國除。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming of Emperor Shun he died; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 of Emperor Shun he died. The state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 明帝十二男：陳貴妃生後廢帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had twelve sons: Consort Chen bore the Later Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had twelve sons. Consort Chen bore the Later Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 謝修儀生皇子法良。

translations.literal: Lady Xie bore Imperial Son Faliang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie bore Imperial Son Faliang.

sentences.zh: 陳昭華生順帝。

translations.literal: Lady Chen bore Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen bore Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 徐婕妤生第四皇子。

translations.literal: Lady Xu bore the fourth imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu bore the fourth imperial son.

sentences.zh: 鄭修容生皇子智井。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng bore Imperial Son Zhijing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng bore Imperial Son Zhijing.

sentences.zh: 次晉熙王燮與皇子法良同生。

translations.literal: Next Prince of Jinxi Xie was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Faliang.
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Xie of Jinxi was born of the same mother as Imperial Son Faliang.

sentences.zh: 泉美人生邵陵殤王友；

translations.literal: Lady Quan bore Prince Shang of Shaoling You;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Quan bore Prince Shang of Shaoling, You.

sentences.zh: 次江夏王躋與第四皇子同生。

translations.literal: next Prince of Jiangxia Ji was born of the same mother as the fourth imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Ji of Jiangxia was born of the same mother as the fourth imperial son.

sentences.zh: 徐良人生武陵王贊。

translations.literal: Lady Xu bore Prince of Wuling Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu bore Prince Zan of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 杜修華生隨陽王翽。

translations.literal: Lady Du bore Prince of Suiyang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Du bore Prince Hui of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 次新興王嵩與武陵王贊同生。

translations.literal: next Prince of Xinxing Song was born of the same mother as Prince of Wuling Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Next Prince Song of Xinxing was born of the same mother as Prince Zan of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 又泉美人生始建王禧。

translations.literal: Also Lady Quan bore Prince of Shijian Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lady Quan bore Prince Xi of Shijian.

sentences.zh: 智井、燮、躋、贊並出繼。

translations.literal: Zhijing, Xie, Ji, and Zan were all given out in adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing, Xie, Ji, and Zan were all given out in adoption.

sentences.zh: 法良未封。

translations.literal: Faliang was not enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang was not enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 第四皇子未有名，早夭。

translations.literal: The fourth imperial son had no name and died early.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth imperial son had no name and died early.

sentences.zh: 邵陵殤王友字仲賢，明帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Shaoling You, styled Zhongxian, was Emperor Ming's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shang of Shaoling, You, styled Zhongxian, was Emperor Ming's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，出為南中郎將、江州刺史，封邵陵王。

translations.literal: At age five he went out as General of the South Center and Governor of Jiang Province, enfeoffed Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: At age five he went out as General of the South Center and governor of Jiang Province, enfeoffed Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年，桂陽王休範誅後，王室微弱，友府州文案及臣吏不諱「有無」之「有」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor, after Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was executed the royal house was weak; in You's prefectural and princely documents and among clerks and officers they did not taboo the "you" in "you wu" (having or not having).
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 2 of the Later Deposed Emperor, after Prince Xiufan of Guiyang was executed the royal house was weak. In You's prefectural and princely documents and among clerks and officers they did not taboo the "you" in "you wu" (having or not having).

sentences.zh: 順帝升明二年，徙南豫州刺史，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming of Emperor Shun he was transferred Governor of South Yu Province and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 of Emperor Shun he was transferred governor of South Yu Province and died.

sentences.zh: 無子國除。

translations.literal: No son — the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: No son — the state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 新興王嵩字仲嶽，明帝第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xinxing Song, styled Zhongyue, was Emperor Ming's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Song of Xinxing, styled Zhongyue, was Emperor Ming's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降封定襄縣公。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Dingxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the Mandate he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Dingxiang county.

sentences.zh: 始建王禧字仲安，明帝第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shijian Xi, styled Zhong'an, was Emperor Ming's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Shijian, styled Zhong'an, was Emperor Ming's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降封荔浦縣公，尋並雲謀反賜死。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Lipu county; shortly both were charged with plotting rebellion and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the Mandate he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Lipu county. Shortly both were charged with plotting rebellion and granted death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：甚矣哉，元嘉之遇禍也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: How extreme was the calamity of the Yuanjia era!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: How extreme was the calamity of the Yuanjia era!

sentences.zh: 殺逆之釁，事起肌膚，因心之童，遂亡天性。

translations.literal: The omen of regicide arose from the skin; the child of the heart's intent thus lost Heaven's nature.
translations.idiomatic: The omen of regicide arose from the skin. The child of the heart's intent thus lost Heaven's nature.

sentences.zh: 雖鳴鏑之酷，未極於斯，其不至覆亡，亦為幸也。

translations.literal: Though the cruelty of whistling arrows did not reach this extreme, that the dynasty did not reach total overthrow was also fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Though the cruelty of whistling arrows did not reach this extreme, that the dynasty did not reach total overthrow was also fortune.

sentences.zh: 明皇統運，疑隙內構，尋斧所加，先自王戚。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's succession met with suspicion and rifts built within; where the axe-edge fell, first were the royal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's succession met with suspicion and rifts built within. Where the axe-edge fell, first were the royal kin.

sentences.zh: 晉刺以獷暴摧軀，巴哀由和良酖體，保身之路，未知攸適。

translations.literal: Prince Ci of Jinping perished by fierce brutality; Prince Ai of Baling was poisoned by harmony and goodness — the road of preserving oneself, one does not know where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ci of Jinping perished by fierce brutality. Prince Ai of Baling was poisoned by harmony and goodness — the road of preserving oneself, one does not know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 昔之戒子，慎勿為善，詳求其旨，將遠有以乎。

translations.literal: The ancients' warning to sons — carefully do not do good — examining the intent in detail, is there perhaps far-reaching reason in this?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients' warning to sons — carefully do not do good — examining the intent in detail, is there perhaps far-reaching reason in this?

sentences.zh: 詩云：「不自我先，不自我後。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "It was not before me, nor after me."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "It was not before me, nor after me."

sentences.zh: 」蓋古人之畏亂也。

translations.literal: Thus the ancients feared disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ancients feared disorder.

sentences.zh: 孝武諸子，提挈以成釁亂，遂至宇內沸騰，王室如毀，而帝之諸胤莫不殲焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's sons were led along until they completed the omen of disorder — thus the realm within boiled and seethed, the royal house as if destroyed, and the Emperor's descendants were none who were not exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's sons were led along until they completed the omen of disorder — thus the realm within boiled and seethed, the royal house as if destroyed, and the emperor's descendants were none who were not exterminated.

sentences.zh: 強不如弱，義在於此。

translations.literal: Strong is not as good as weak — righteousness lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: Strong is not as good as weak — righteousness lies in this.

sentences.zh: 明帝負螟之慶，事非己出，枝葉不茂，豈能庇其本乎。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming enjoyed the blessing of the horned moth — the affair was not of his own issue; branches and leaves were not lush — how could he shelter the root?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming enjoyed the blessing of the horned moth — the affair was not of his own issue. Branches and leaves were not lush — how could he shelter the root?
